jobs.title: Claims Analyst
jobs.jd: Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam. We’re hiring a Claims Analyst to own the day-to-day integrity of our claims and adjudication workflows and to help build the processes, controls, and reporting behind them. This is a hands-on role: you’ll personally work our hardest claims and denials while standing up the playbooks, benchmarks, and dashboards that let claims operations scale without breaking. Reporting to our Manager, RCM, you’ll sit at the intersection of our clearinghouse, prior-auth, and finance systems — and you’ll be the person who can explain exactly why a claim paid, denied, or landed where it did. What you'll do: Own claims adjudication and QA. Review, validate, and adjudicate imaging claims against benefit designs, contracted rates, and our pass-through payment model; identify and resolve pricing, coding, and eligibility discrepancies before they become client or member issues. Lead denials management. Investigate root causes of denials and underpayments, drive appeals and resubmissions, and build recurring analysis that turns denial patterns into fixes upstream (prior auth, eligibility, EDI configuration). Manage EDI and clearinghouse workflows. Work hands-on in Waystar across 837P submissions, 835 remittances, and companion-guide requirements; troubleshoot rejections and payer-specific edits; partner with vendors to keep the pipes clean. Safeguard cost-share and accumulator accuracy. Ensure deductible, coinsurance, HDHP, and accumulator logic is applied correctly so members and clients are billed accurately and we stay compliant with cost-sharing rules. Own AR and aging. Monitor accounts receivable and claims aging, prioritize collectible balances, and maintain reporting that gives finance and leadership a real-time view of what’s outstanding and why. Build the reporting layer. Develop and maintain dashboards and KPIs (adjudication turnaround, denial rate, clean-claim rate, AR aging, recovery rate) from Waystar and adjacent claims data. Coordinate across the stack. Work closely with prior authorization (Infinx), finance, and client-facing teams to close the loop between authorization, exam, claim, and payment. Write the playbook. Document repeatable SOPs, edits, and escalation paths, and help train and mentor analysts as the team grows. About you: Required 2+ years in healthcare claims, revenue cycle, or medical billing, with demonstrated ownership of complex adjudication and denials work Deep hands-on experience with EDI transactions (837/835) and a clearinghouse platform (Waystar strongly preferred) Strong command of CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10, place-of-service, and modifier logic — ideally in radiology/imaging Working knowledge of benefit structures, cost-sharing, deductibles, and accumulator/HDHP mechanics Advanced spreadsheet skills and comfort building reporting from raw claims data A meticulous, audit-minded approach: you can trace any dollar to its source and defend it Preferred Experience at a TPA, benefits administrator, or payer, especially serving self-funded employers Familiarity with prior authorization workflows and tools (e.g., Infinx) Exposure to appeals, payer escalations, and underpayment recovery at scale Early-stage or high-growth environment experience — comfortable building process where none exists The salary range for this position is $50,000 - $65,000. This position is also bonus eligible. Individual compensation will depend on various factors, including qualifications, skills, experience, location, and applicable laws. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible to participate in our equity incentive and competitive benefits plans. Fraud and Security Notice: Please be aware of recent job scam attempts. jobs.jd: Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Analyst, Risk Adjustment to join our Risk Adjustment team. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family. Accurate and complete clinical documentation helps ensure that a member’s health status is appropriately represented. Prospective Risk Adjustment focuses on proactively supporting opportunities for healthcare providers to review members’ health information and accurately document conditions addressed during clinical care, in accordance with applicable clinical coding and documentation requirements. These efforts may include sharing relevant clinical information with providers at the point of care, conducting virtual or in-home health assessments, and providing reports that identify historical or suspected conditions for provider review and clinical validation. The Analyst, Risk Adjustment supports the day-to-day execution and performance of Prospective Risk Adjustment programs. This role partners with internal teams and external vendors to ensure operational workflows are functioning as intended, program data and reporting are accurate, claims are processed appropriately, and operational issues are identified and resolved in a timely manner. The analyst will support a portfolio of initiatives including Point-of-Care tools, Virtual Health Assessments (VHA), In-Home Assessments (IHA), and provider reporting to support the review of member conditions. This role is well suited for an analytical, detail-oriented professional interested in developing expertise in Risk Adjustment and healthcare operations. You will report into the Sr. Manager, Strategic Initiatives (Risk Adjustment). Work Location: This position is based in our New York, NY office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. jobs.title: Intelligence Systems Analyst
jobs.jd:
About the Team

The Intelligence and Investigations (I2) team provides intelligence to decision makers across OpenAI and investigates severe misuse of our products. I2’s work saves lives: we disrupt real-world violence, protect children, and prevent catastrophic harms from AI misuse. We also draw on our investigations and in-depth analysis of a wide range of data sources to provide actionable quantitative and qualitative intelligence to OpenAI’s leadership.

I2 Engineering works hand in hand with I2’s analysts and investigators, building tools that expand what human experts can understand and accomplish. Our tools help them make sense of vast and complex datasets, discover and measure on-platform and off-platform risk, and investigate severe misuse with greater speed, depth, and consistency.


About the Role

We are looking for an Intelligence Systems Analyst who wants to work alongside investigators to understand difficult cases, contribute to analysis, and build tools and workflows that help the team do more. As investigators pursue leads, assess risks, and determine what happened, you’ll see where better tools could help and build them.

The role combines hands-on software and data work with meaningful participation in investigations. Depending on the problem, you might trace activity across internal systems, write a query or small application, prototype an AI-assisted workflow, improve how evidence is assembled, or turn an investigator’s recurring need into a durable product capability.

You will work closely with engineers, analysts, investigators, and other subject matter experts. Success requires enough operational understanding to contribute meaningfully to an investigation and enough technical ownership to build solutions that remain useful after the immediate case is resolved.


In this role, you will:

 - Work directly alongside investigators on complex cases, helping develop leads, analyze evidence, and identify useful technical approaches.

 - Build and maintain software, data workflows, and internal tools that accelerate investigations of potential high-severity misuse or harm.

 - Use Python, SQL, and internal data systems to gather, connect, and analyze information relevant to investigative work.

 - Apply OpenAI’s models to research, search, triage, synthesis, and evidence review in workflows that keep expert investigators informed and in control.

 - Turn recurring investigative bottlenecks into reliable tools, automation, and product capabilities that support multiple users and cases.

 - Prototype quickly when a new investigative question arises, then improve reliability, usability, and maintainability as requirements become clearer.

 - Respect the privacy, permissions, evidence-handling requirements, and operational safeguards that accompany sensitive investigative work.

 - Collaborate with teams across Applied, Safety Systems, Research, User Operations, and Strategy when their expertise or systems are needed.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Experience building and shipping software, internal tools, data workflows, or operational products.

 - Comfort working directly with investigators, analysts, or other subject matter experts in ambiguous or consequential situations.

 - Practical experience with Python, SQL, and structured or unstructured data.

 - The ability to investigate an unclear problem, follow evidence across systems, and turn what you learn into a practical next step.

 - Sound judgment about privacy, data access, evidence quality, and the consequences of getting an investigation wrong.

 - Interest in using AI systems to extend human investigative capability while keeping expert judgment central.

 - The flexibility to move between coding, analysis, investigative support, and close collaboration with technical and operational partners.

Experience in trust and safety, security, intelligence, investigations, or related domains is helpful but not required.

jobs.title: AI Research Resident (Algorithms Codesign)
jobs.jd:
NORMAL COMPUTING | BUILD WITH US

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.


THE RESIDENCY PROGRAM

The AI Research Residency is Normal Computing's flagship program for exceptional researchers and engineers who want to work at the frontier of AI. Residents join a small, hand-picked cohort with a dedicated research mentor, direct access to the team developing the algorithms for our in-memory inference hardware, and a clear arc from onboarding through publication.

Every residency is built around two milestones that mark you as part of something bigger than a single project: a research paper co-authored with our team, and a company-wide research colloquium where you present your findings to the full Normal Computing organization. You'll leave with a body of published, presented work, and a standing as one of the earliest residents to help define what this program becomes.


THIS TRACK: ALGORITHMS CODESIGN

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. This track is about the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it: rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip.

You'll work on this as a co-design problem. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, so your findings feed architectural decisions rather than implementing against a fixed specification. You'll validate ideas against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.


YOUR NORMAL EXPERIENCE

This is a hands-on research residency: you'll take ownership of a real technical problem in inference algorithms for in-memory compute, work alongside the researchers and engineers building our platform, and be expected to contribute ideas, not just execute someone else's. Your job is to help turn research into production-quality research code that a team can build on. Outside-of-the-box thinking is encouraged.

You'll get direct exposure to the pace, ambiguity, and speed of decision-making that comes with working at a fast-moving, well-funded startup, where the distance between an idea on a whiteboard and a result on real hardware is measured in weeks, not years.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Develop inference algorithms for in-memory hardware. Understand which parts of LLM workloads are best suited to in-memory execution and develop algorithms that exploit it natively, demonstrated first in simulation and then on hardware.

Design numerical methods that fit the physics. Design methods that exploit thermal noise and analog dynamics rather than working around them.

Build evaluation suites and benchmarks. Help build the evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that characterize how algorithms behave on real hardware and in simulation, and tell us honestly whether any of it actually works.

Translate workloads into hardware constraints. Turn insights about model workloads into constraints and opportunities for the hardware and architecture teams.

Prototype and iterate rapidly. Move with the hardware as it evolves from simulation to FPGA to silicon.

Drive a research question of your own. Partner with researchers and engineers to scope, run, and iterate on an original technical investigation, with rigorous experimental analysis and documentation along the way.

Co-author a paper. Work with the team to write up your findings for submission to a relevant venue, with mentorship on framing, experiments, and technical writing. One of the two milestones every resident builds toward.

Present at the residency colloquium. Share your work and thinking with the broader Normal Computing research community at the program's capstone event, and get real-time feedback from people building this technology every day.


WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU A GREAT FIT

Currently pursuing or recently completed a graduate degree (MS or PhD, or equivalent research experience) in machine learning, applied mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field. Publications are a strong plus, but not required at the resident level; a solid research track record is what matters.

A working understanding of large model inference: attention mechanisms, KV cache, long-context decoding, memory bandwidth constraints. Deep production experience isn't expected at the resident level, but the intuition should feel familiar.

Some exposure to inference optimization (quantization, sparsity, kernel fusion, or memory-efficient attention), or to stochastic systems, probabilistic methods, numerical analysis, or analog computation.

Strong Python skills, plus some experience with a systems language (C++, Rust, or similar) or with implementing algorithms close to hardware, beyond high-level frameworks.

Some experience (course projects, research, or otherwise) turning a research idea into working, reasonably reproducible code. You care about whether results replicate, not just whether a demo works once.

Comfort reasoning from first principles about what a novel substrate can do efficiently.

Bonus: exposure to analog or mixed-signal systems, in-memory compute, or non-von-Neumann architectures; publications or open-source work in efficient inference, stochastic algorithms, or novel computing; or experience working on hardware that did not yet exist when you joined.

Strong written and verbal communication skills; prior experience writing up research (papers, theses, technical reports) is a plus, as is any experience presenting technical work to a live audience.

A bias toward ownership and self-direction. You're energized, not overwhelmed, by the ambiguity and speed of a small, fast-moving startup.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Acquisition
jobs.jd:
Superhuman offers a dynamic hybrid working model for this role. This flexible approach gives team members the best of both worlds: plenty of focus time along with in-person collaboration that helps foster trust, innovation, and a strong team culture.




ABOUT SUPERHUMAN

Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. The Superhuman suite of apps and agents brings AI wherever people work, integrating with over 1 million applications and websites. The company's products include Grammarly's writing assistance, Docs’ collaborative workspace, Mail's inbox management, and Go, the proactive AI assistant that understands context and delivers help automatically. Founded in 2009, Superhuman empowers over 40 million people, 50,000 organizations, and 3,000 educational institutions worldwide to eliminate busywork and focus on what matters. Learn more at superhuman.com http://superhuman.com and about our values here https://superhuman.com/company/values.




THE OPPORTUNITY

Turn complex data into growth decisions that shape the future of Superhuman’s product suite.

As an Acquisition Data Scientist at Superhuman, you’ll shape how we acquire, activate, and expand our user base across a diverse portfolio of consumer and enterprise products. You’ll partner directly with Acquisition Marketing to improve the effectiveness of paid and organic channels, optimize the web funnel, and ensure every marketing dollar drives measurable growth.

Your work will span the Superhuman product suite, including Grammarly, Mail, Docs, Databases, GPTZero, Fathom, and Go. Because we’re building an integrated platform rather than a collection of standalone tools, insights from one product can unlock growth across the portfolio. You’ll tackle questions spanning budget allocation, channel attribution, SEO, AEO, cross-product activation, bundled offerings, and the full self-serve journey from first touch through activation and viral expansion.

You’ll be embedded in a cross-functional pod aligned to a Route to Market, working closely with Engineering, Finance, Marketing, Design, and User Research. With direct access to the leaders setting strategy, you’ll serve as the go-to data partner for acquisition: getting into the technical details, translating complex findings into clear recommendations on channel optimization, budget decisions, and new growth areas.

This role is for a hands-on data scientist who thrives in a fast-moving environment, enjoys solving complex growth problems, and wants their work to measurably influence outcomes across products, audiences, and go-to-market motions.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Be the go-to data person working directly with our Acquisition Marketing team, helping drive the efficacy of their marketing spend across our core paid and organic channels. This role is for someone who wants to be extremely hands-on, enjoys partnering cross-functionally with marketing peers, and wants to get deep into the technical weeds to find the best recommendations to ensure we optimize every marketing dollar we spend.

 - Be the embedded data science partner for the Superhuman Acquisition Marketing team — shaping channel strategy, budget allocation, prioritization, and roadmap decisions with evidence, not just fielding ad hoc requests.

 - Define and own the metrics that matter for Acquisition: LTV/CAC, new user growth, lifetime value, and web conversion rates to ensure we are responsible with our ad spend and driving continued conversion optimization.

 - Design and run incrementality tests across our most critical acquisition channels like Google, Meta, and YouTube.

 - Find opportunities for new user growth through budget reinvestment, new acquisition sources, international expansion, and website optimization.

 - Partner with our Acquisition, Engineering, Design, User Research, and Finance teams to build functional roadmaps for optimization of our acquisition channels across paid and organic sources.

 - Use data to craft a narrative, tell a story, and influence decisions to improve the efficiency of our ad channels and drive meaningful new user growth.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - You have 7+ years of data science experience and a track record of driving measurable impact for business and customers.

 - Advanced expertise in experimentation and causal inference, including designing incrementality tests and translating results into acquisition investment decisions.

 - Demonstrated ability to develop marketing mix and budget allocation models that measure channel effectiveness, identify diminishing returns, and optimize acquisition spend across channels.

 - You have strong applied statistics skills and machine learning skills, and you use them to drive product and growth decisions.

 - You influence cross-functional partners and turn technical insight into action through clear communication, empathetic building, and openness to ideas from anywhere.

 - You’re a self-starting, creative problem-solver who distills problems to their core and thrives with ambiguity.

 - You’re comfortable using AI-assisted development tools like Claude Code or Codex to move faster, and you have the judgment to validate and supervise their output.

 - You have a bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (statistics, mathematics, economics, computer science, data science, or a similar field); an advanced degree or equivalent practical experience is preferred.

Nice to haves:

 - Familiarity working with ad platforms across Google, Meta, and YouTube.

 - Experience with SEO and AEO optimization and organic acquisition channels.

 - You’re familiar with experimentation platforms such as Statsig and modern data stacks such as Databricks.

 - You have experience working at a fast-growing startup, on AI-native consumer products, and/or in B2B/SaaS.




COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Superhuman offers all team members competitive pay along with a benefits package encompassing the following and more:

 - Excellent health care (including a wide range of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and fertility benefits)

 - Disability and life insurance options

 - 401(k) matching

 - Paid parental leave

 - 20 days of paid time off per year, 12 days of paid holidays per year, two floating holidays per year, and flexible sick time

 - Generous stipends (including those for caregiving, pet care, wellness, your home office, and more)

 - Annual professional development budget and opportunities

Superhuman takes a market-based approach to compensation, which means base pay may vary depending on your location. Our US locations are categorized into two compensation zones based on proximity to our hub locations.

Base pay may vary considerably depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The expected salary ranges for this position are outlined below by compensation zone and may be modified in the future.




WE ENCOURAGE YOU TO APPLY

At Superhuman, we value our differences, and we encourage all to apply—especially those whose identities are traditionally underrepresented in tech organizations. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected by law. Superhuman is an equal opportunity employer and a participant in the US federal E-Verify program (US). We also abide by the Employment Equity Act (Canada).

AI is unleashing the biggest wave of company creation in history. Clay's mission is to be the engine those companies use to grow to their full potential.

Clay predicts the next best action for your business and then helps you take it. We started by aggregating the best data for B2B companies. Hear from our employees directly on our Glassdoor https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-Clay-EI_IE9850794.11,15.htm page!

 


GROWTH STRATEGIST, KEY @ CLAY

We’re building a new Key Accounts team within Clay’s Strategic GS segment. It’s a senior team dedicated to Clay’s largest and highest-potential customers.

You’ll be a strategic partner to a small number of the world’s most influential companies, including Fortune 500 enterprises and leading AI companies. You’ll help their revenue operations and marketing leaders change how they go to market with Clay. As a founding member, you’ll also help define how this segment engages, retains, and grows Clay’s most important relationships.

What You’ll Do

 - Own a focused portfolio. Be the senior owner of a handful of strategic accounts, and the person who knows each one best.

 - Lead GTM transformation. Set a multi-year vision with executive teams, define the jobs to be done, and drive adoption across business units, regions, and functions.

 - Build C-suite relationships. Be a trusted advisor to CROs, CMOs, and other executives, and keep Clay central to their GTM strategy.

 - Deliver value in P&L terms. Define success metrics with leadership, measure them through data, surveys, and interviews, and present the business impact in executive business reviews.

 - Quarterback the account team. Coordinate Sales, Solutions, Support, Product, and Engineering to run complex programs, handle escalations, and manage risk.

 - Own renewals, co-own growth. Partner with Sales to anticipate needs, deepen use cases, and expand into new teams through cross-sell and upsell.

 - Shape the product. Represent Clay’s most influential customers internally and directly influence the roadmap.

What You’ll Bring

 - Experience: 8–10+ years in strategic account management, customer success, or transformation consulting with Fortune 500 or similarly complex global organizations.

 - Transformation track record: You’ve built C-suite relationships and led large-scale technology adoption or change programs.

 - Commercial results: You’ve owned renewals and consistently hit iARR and GRR targets.

 - Strategic thinking: You set a vision, build frameworks, and turn product capabilities into measurable business outcomes.

 - Executive presence: You stay calm presenting to senior leaders, in high-stakes situations, and in conflict.

 - Cross-functional leadership: You lead without formal authority, both inside Clay and inside the customer’s organization.

 - Technical curiosity: You want to understand the product deeply enough to connect what’s possible with what the customer needs.

 - Builder mentality: You’re energized by shaping a new team’s operating model from the ground up.

 - Nice to have: A background in management consulting or strategy advisory.

jobs.title: Researcher II, Weekend Team
jobs.jd:
At WHOOP, we’re on a mission to unlock human performance and healthspan. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies, behaviors, and daily lives.

 

WHOOP Labs is the on-site research facility for product development and innovation at WHOOP. We conduct human-centered hardware and algorithm research to create best-in-class product experiences that work for all members.

 

WHOOP is hiring a Researcher II to support research planning and execution on weekends, supporting critical data collection windows for participant diversity and expanded access. This role will cover a broad range of research studies for algorithm training, hardware validation, and design testing. While your home base will be WHOOP’s on-site product research facility, WHOOP Labs, studies will include field collections across the metro Boston area to widen access for diverse communities. Your efforts will support the organization as we continue to develop a best-in-class experience and lead the wearables industry.

 

*This role is fully onsite at our Boston, MA office and follows a 4x10 schedule, with four 10-hour workdays each week, Friday through Monday, and three days off Tuesday through Thursday.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Execute testing protocols across multiple concurrent studies, owning research execution on weekends and collaborating with other researchers on Friday and Monday to ensure consistent protocol administration across all days and shifts.

 - Own research documentation for weekend hours, collaborating with other researchers on Friday and Monday to ensure effective handoffs and information transfer across shifts.

 - Provide coaching and guidance to participants during exercise protocols, balancing data integrity, research best practices, and participant experience

 - Create a supportive and welcoming environment for participants engaging in a range of research tasks, from exercises to device interactions

 - Manage the use, troubleshooting, and upkeep of sensitive data collection equipment and prototype devices

 - Develop strong working knowledge of WHOOP’s research platform tooling suite, with the ability to troubleshoot issues in real time—including during active data collections—and problem-solve on the fly

 - Develop junior researchers by providing technical coaching, delegation, constructive feedback, and growth opportunities

 - Own daily lab management tasks required for data collections to be successful, such as laundry, equipment cleaning, material organization, and overall lab readiness

 - Serve as an ambassador for WHOOP Labs and the WHOOP brand

 

QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s Degree in human physiology, biomedical engineering, psychology, HCI, or similar

 - Professional experience in research & development, human subjects research, or a related field, including 2+ years of experience conducting human subjects research

 - Strong technological background and working knowledge of data management systems including the Google Suite

 - Familiarity with research platform tools and hardware testing environments preferred

 - Strong interpersonal communication skills with a savvy for working as part of a highly collaborative, fast-paced team

 - Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt quickly in dynamic research settings

 - Prior experience in customer service or other public-facing roles a plus

 - Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, with confidence giving and receiving feedback across disciplines

 

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify to determine employment eligibility. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.

At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $75,000 - $95,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.

In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

These ranges may be modified in the future to reflect evolving market conditions and organizational needs. While most offers will typically fall toward the starting point of the range, total compensation will depend on the candidate’s specific qualifications, expertise, and alignment with the role’s requirements.

jobs.title: Security Analyst
jobs.jd:
At WHOOP, we are on a mission to unlock human performance and extend healthspan. The security organization supports this mission by protecting the systems, data, and infrastructure that power the platform and enable trusted member experiences.

WHOOP is seeking a Security Analyst to support day-to-day security operations and maintain operational visibility across the security environment. This role works closely with the internal security team and external security partners to investigate alerts, coordinate response activities, and ensure security issues are triaged and addressed efficiently.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical skills with operational discipline and enjoys working across security and engineering teams to investigate potential threats and improve security processes.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Triage and investigate security alerts originating from internal security tooling as well as those escalated by external security monitoring partners.

 - Monitor and manage the internal security operations ticket queue, ensuring alerts and investigations are prioritized, tracked, and resolved in a timely manner.

 - Assist with investigation of security events across endpoint, identity, cloud, and SaaS platforms.

 - Support incident response activities including investigation, containment coordination, documentation, and post-incident analysis.

 - Respond to external threat intelligence and digital risk alerts related to potential brand abuse, impersonation, or exposed credentials.

 - Collaborate with security engineering teams and external security partners to improve detection coverage and reduce false positives.

 - Help identify gaps in logging, telemetry, or investigation workflows across security platforms.

 - Assist with threat hunting and security investigations using data from SIEM and other security tools.

 - Support vulnerability management workflows by assisting with triage, prioritization, and tracking of remediation activities.

 - Own and manage the security operations queue while serving as a central intake point for security questions, alerts, and reports across the organization, ensuring items are triaged, prioritized, and driven through investigation or resolution.

 - Operate the organization’s phishing simulation program to reduce susceptibility to social engineering threats, including managing phishing campaigns and coordinating targeted remediation training for users with repeated failures.

 - Identify opportunities to improve security operations through process improvements, automation, and responsible use of AI to streamline investigation, triage, and reporting workflows.

 - Maintain documentation for incident response procedures, investigation workflows, and operational playbooks.

 - Participate in the security team’s on-call rotation to support investigation and response activities when needed.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, threat detection, or a related cybersecurity role.

 - Experience investigating security alerts or suspicious activity across environments such as endpoint, identity, cloud, or SaaS systems.

 - Experience triaging and managing security investigation workflows, including ticket queues or incident tracking systems.

 - Familiarity with SIEM platforms, log analysis, and security monitoring tools.

 - Understanding of common attacker techniques and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.

 - Experience working with security tools such as EDR platforms, identity systems, cloud logging platforms, or similar technologies.

 - Familiarity with modern AI-enabled tools used in enterprise environments and an understanding of risks associated.

 - Experience improving security operations through automation, scripting, or responsible use of AI to increase operational efficiency.

 - Strong analytical and investigative skills with the ability to evaluate security events and determine potential impact.

 - Ability to coordinate investigations across multiple teams and communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Strong written documentation skills for incident records, investigation notes, and operational procedures.

 - Relevant security certifications such as Security+, CySA+, SSCP, GSEC, or GCIH are a plus.
   
   
   
   This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.
   
   Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.
   
   WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify  https://www.e-verify.gov/to determine employment eligibility
   
   The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.
   
   At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

jobs.title: AI Trainer (Contractor), Voice and Speech Evaluation - USA
jobs.jd:
About Inworld

Inworld is a research lab and inference provider focused on realtime AI for consumer-facing applications. We build first-party speech models, serve LLMs, and run the inference behind modular APIs designed for high-volume, realtime workloads.

Hundreds of millions of users interact with Inworld powered apps every day and we serve over 10 trillion LLM tokens per month. Our models and infrastructure support consumer applications across companions, healthcare, fitness, education, media, and more. Our work spans model research, realtime inference, large-scale serving infrastructure, and the APIs developers use to bring these capabilities into production.

We’ve raised more than $125M from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Section 32, Kleiner Perkins, Microsoft’s M12 venture fund, Founders Fund, Meta, Stanford, and others. Our technology has powered experiences from companies including NVIDIA, Microsoft Xbox, Niantic, Logitech Streamlabs, Wishroll, Little Umbrella, and Bible Chat. Inworld has also been recognized by CB Insights as one of the 100 most promising AI companies globally and named one of LinkedIn’s Top 10 Startups in the USA.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Listen to paired or grouped speech samples and judge which sounds more natural, expressive, or faithful to instructions

 - Score voices against rubrics for naturalness, clarity, emotion, pacing, and delivery style

 - Label voice attributes such as perceived gender, age, accent or dialect, and tone, and flag mismatches with existing metadata

 - Judge how closely cloned voices match their source speaker

 - Review batches of new voices for audio quality and suitability before public release

 - Test new speech features in pre-release environments and report bugs, edge cases, and usability issues

 - Write clear, structured findings that engineers can act on

 - For multilingual roles: evaluate pronunciation, dialect accuracy, and naturalness in your native language


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - A trained ear. Background in audio production, broadcast, voice acting, music, linguistics, phonetics, or similar

 - Ability to hear and describe subtle differences in prosody, timing, pronunciation, and audio quality

 - Consistent, careful judgment across large batches of similar samples

 - Comfort with beta web tools, VPN access, and spreadsheets, and willingness to troubleshoot minor access issues

 - Strong written English for reporting findings

 - Ability to turn tasks around within a day when needed, including occasional weekend availability


NICE TO HAVE

 - Native or near-native fluency in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, Brazilian Portuguese, or a regional Spanish dialect

 - Experience with TTS, voice AI, dubbing, or localization QA

 - Familiarity with A/B evaluation or annotation work


Location: Remote within the United States. 

Compensation: $20-$55 per hour. Rate depends on region and language specialty.



Inworld Jobs Privacy https://inworld.ai/jobs-privacy

jobs.title: Part-Time AI Research Data Annotator
jobs.jd:
AI RESEARCH DATA ANNOTATOR (PART-TIME)

Location: San Francisco, CA (On-site)
Type: Part-time contract, approximately 15–20 hours per week
Compensation: $20–$25/hour




ABOUT ENGRAMME

Engramme is an AI research lab building Large Memory Models (LMMs) to give people perfect, infinite memory.

We're founded by Gabriel Kreiman, a former Harvard professor, and Spandan Madan, a former Harvard researcher. We're a small, ambitious team in San Francisco working on one of the most fundamental challenges in AI: memory.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for part-time AI Research Evaluators / Data Annotators to help us train, evaluate, and improve our AI memory system.

Our technology connects information from everyday digital tools—such as email, messages, and documents—and surfaces relevant memories when they're useful.

You'll work directly with our research team on a variety of data labeling and evaluation tasks. These tasks are essential to developing and improving our Large Memory Models.



Examples of tasks include:

 - AI Memory Evaluation: Use Engramme's AI memory system during everyday digital activities and evaluate whether the memories it retrieves are relevant and useful.

 - Conversation Annotation: Review transcripts of recorded conversations and identify specific statements, facts, experiences, and other information that represent memories.

 - Memory Classification: Examine AI-generated memories and classify them based on criteria such as whether they contain spam, irrelevant information, or other undesirable content.

 - Research Data Annotation: Label and categorize different types of memory-related information to help researchers develop and train new algorithms.

 - Research Experiments: Participate in structured experiments, which may include recorded conversations with appropriate consent, and assist with other emerging data collection and labeling tasks.

Because we're developing a new category of AI, the specific tasks will evolve over time. You'll receive instructions and training for each task and work closely with our researchers to refine how memory data is evaluated and annotated.



This is a hands-on data evaluation and annotation role, not a software engineering or AI research scientist position.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Complete a variety of data annotation and evaluation tasks during scheduled in-office sessions.

 - Review text, conversation transcripts, and AI-generated memories to produce accurate, consistent labels.

 - Use Engramme's memory system during everyday digital activities and provide feedback on the relevance and usefulness of retrieved memories.

 - Apply task-specific annotation guidelines and exercise judgment when encountering ambiguous information.

 - Complete a high volume of careful, consistent annotations while maintaining quality standards.

 - Identify unclear instructions, edge cases, and recurring issues, and share observations with our research team.

 - Adapt to new annotation tasks as our research priorities and experiments evolve.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong attention to detail: You can carefully examine information and make consistent, well-reasoned judgments.

 - Reliability and consistency: You're comfortable performing repetitive tasks accurately over extended periods.

 - Good judgment: You can interpret nuanced instructions and recognize when an example is ambiguous or requires clarification.

 - Adaptability: You're comfortable learning new tasks and working with guidelines that may evolve as our research progresses.

 - Digital literacy: You're comfortable using web browsers, email, messaging applications, and other everyday digital tools.

 - Clear communication: You can explain your reasoning, flag unclear cases, and provide constructive feedback.

 - Availability: You can work approximately 15–20 hours per week in person at our San Francisco office.

 - Must be at least 18 years old.

Some evaluation tasks may involve connecting your own digital information to our system, subject to informed consent and appropriate privacy protections.

No prior AI, programming, or research experience is required. College students and recent graduates are welcome to apply.




WHY JOIN US?

 - Contribute directly to cutting-edge AI research and help develop a new category of AI technology.

 - Work alongside researchers and engineers developing Large Memory Models.

 - Gain firsthand exposure to how AI systems are trained, evaluated, and improved.

 - Help shape annotation guidelines and evaluation methods for an emerging area of AI research.

 - Enjoy flexible part-time scheduling and a collaborative in-office environment.

jobs.title: Founding Strategic Finance
jobs.jd:
FOUNDING STRATEGIC FINANCE



About Sela

Sela is the market-leading AI voice agent for mortgage lenders. Founded in 2024, we’ve grown like crazy (~$0→14M in 21 months), and currently count 6 of the 10 largest independent mortgage banks in the U.S. as enterprise customers. If we’re successful, the cost of owning a home in the US will become ~1% cheaper. We’ve raised $21M+ across our Seed and Series A from top investors.



Why This Is a Huge Opportunity

Around 1% of the U.S. labor force works in phone sales, representing roughly $100B of annual salary, and the industry is poised at the brink of complete disruption. We are at the cutting edge of this economic transformation, one of the first companies creating real, durable economic value through applied AI.

Buying a house is the largest financial decision most people make in their lives, and homeownership is tied to many other purchases, including life insurance, homeowners insurance, alarm systems, home renovations, solar panels, and more. By owning the mortgage vertical, we will own the relationship with the consumer, allowing us to serve as the essential AI infrastructure for high-consideration consumer sales.



Why Join

Explosive growth: The market pull is exhilarating. We’ve grown 10x in the past 12 months and more than 100x since our seed round, all without a dedicated sales or marketing team. Building something that people want so badly is the best feeling you can have in a startup.

Team and culture: We are a high-agency team where the bar is high and everyone makes the people around them better. Collaboration and intensity are core team values: people truly care about their work and their coworkers. At the same time, we don’t take ourselves too seriously.

Challenging problems: Outperforming human sales teams on half a million daily calls is not easy. Low-latency, real-time infra. 99.9% uptime. Enterprise-grade privacy and security. Advanced simulation and evaluation systems. Flexible A/B testing. AI scheduler and dialer. We own the whole stack and we do not compromise on quality.

Well-funded: We’ve raised $21M+ in total funding, most recently a $15M Series A in June 2026.



The Role

Sela’s AI voice agents hold real conversations with real people on behalf of some of the largest mortgage lenders in the country. We are looking for a Founding Strategic Finance lead to help us build the finance function that scales with it.

You’ll report directly to the CEO and work on decisions that shape the business, from how we price large enterprise deals to how we plan and where we invest. One day you’re deep in the P&L model, the next you’re prepping the board deck or reviewing a contract. You’ll help decide what gets measured, how we forecast, and which systems we put in place along the way.



What You’ll Own

Planning & modeling

 - Build and own the company’s operating model (revenue, gross margin, cost structure, headcount, and cash) and turn it into the plan the founders run the business against

 - Model core revenue drivers: customer-level usage trends, net revenue retention, upsell and cross-sell

Pricing & deals

 - Design pricing and deal structures for some of the largest mortgage lenders in the country, and partner with sales on every enterprise negotiation

 - Build the sales capacity model and design the commission plans for our first AE team

Board & investors

 - Own the board deck and the financial narrative to investors, and help lead preparation for our next raise

Finance infrastructure

 - Build quote-to-cash from scratch, from contract to invoice to collections, so usage-based enterprise revenue is billed accurately and on time

 - Be the financial reviewer on every commercial contract, working with outside counsel and advisors

 - Choose and stand up the finance stack (systems, vendors, outside accountants) and set the processes the finance team will run on as it grows



What We’re Looking For

Must-haves

 - 2+ years in startup finance, or 3+ years total experience with a strong FP&A background

 - Hands-on experience with core P&L work, AE models, and commission plans

 - Structured thinking and strong judgment. You can take a messy question, break it down, and get to a recommendation without being handed a framework.

 - A clear, effective communicator who can work with founders, sales, legal, and vendors, and present to a board

 - High ownership and initiative. You’re comfortable operating without a fully developed playbook and figuring out what works.

 - The ability to thrive in a fast-moving environment where the product, market, and business are all evolving quickly

Nice-to-haves

 - B2B SaaS background where you’ve seen what a scaling finance function looks like

 - Experience with usage-based pricing or revenue models

 - Experience managing billing systems or other finance vendors

 - Comfort reviewing commercial contracts

 - Exposure to mortgage, lending, or another regulated financial services vertical



Benefits

 - 150k–250k salary

 - Top-of-market medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents

 - 401(k) with a top-of-market employer match

 - Unlimited PTO

 - Hybrid in-office schedule: four days a week together in SF, with a flexible remote day on Wednesdays

jobs.title: Client Service Analyst, Embedded Finance
jobs.jd: Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv. We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv. Job Title Client Service Analyst, Embedded Finance What does a successful Client Service Analyst in Embedded Finance do at Fiserv? The Client Service Analyst is a client-focused service professional who owns the day-to-day oversight of incoming client requests, tickets, and inquiries. Using Client360 and related platform interfaces, this analyst role monitors the full request lifecycle, validates priority and business impact, performs initial analysis and remediation, and routes work to the appropriate Product, Operations, or Technology team when specialized support is required. This role maintains clear client communication, removes barriers to resolution, and uses operational data to improve responsiveness, accountability, and the overall client experience. This is a hands-on service management role that requires technical aptitude and strong analytical skills; it is not primarily a coding, engineering, or infrastructure position. What you will do: Monitor the Client360 queue across assigned clients, ensuring new inquiries are reviewed promptly, accurately categorized, and actively managed through closure. Assess request urgency, severity, client impact, required information, and potential SLA risk; prioritize and escalate work based on documented support processes. Perform initial triage using existing platform tools, administrative interfaces, reports, logs, knowledge articles, and documented procedures to resolve issues when possible. Assign or coordinate requests with the appropriate Product, Operations, Client Services, Technology, or third-party team, maintaining clear ownership and follow-through. Serve as a central point of coordination for client inquiries, providing concise, timely updates, clarifying next steps, and confirming that the client understands the final resolution before closure. Proactively identify aging, stalled, reopened, high-severity, or SLA-at-risk items and drive action plans, escalations, and leadership visibility until resolved. Analyze queue data to identify recurring issues, routing gaps, workload trends, and process improvement opportunities; recommend corrective actions and track outcomes. Maintain accurate ticket documentation, including business impact, troubleshooting completed, decisions, dependencies, owners, target dates, client communications, and closure details. Develop practical dashboards, scorecards, and reporting views using Excel and available enterprise reporting tools; support Power BI reporting where applicable. Help improve intake standards, queue-management practices, escalation paths, knowledge content, and repeatable service procedures across the team. What you will need to have: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Technology, Operations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. 3+ years of experience in client service, technical support, service operations, incident or request management, production support, or a related environment. Demonstrated experience owning or coordinating a case-management or ticket queue and working across teams to drive issues to resolution. Working knowledge of ticket triage, severity assessment, escalation practices, service metrics, and SLA or service-target monitoring. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify trends, exceptions, bottlenecks, and actions from operational data. Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, formulas, charts, data validation, and repeatable reporting. Comfort learning and navigating multiple enterprise tools and platform interfaces; direct Client360 experience is preferred but not required. Ability to manage competing priorities, maintain attention to detail, and follow through in a fast-paced, client-facing environment. What would be great to have: Experience with Client360, ServiceNow, CRM, case-management, or comparable service platforms. Experience creating dashboards or visual reports in Microsoft Power BI. Background in financial services, payments, banking, fintech, or embedded finance. Experience supporting client operational reviews, service scorecards, or executive-level reporting. Knowledge of continuous-improvement methods and the ability to document repeatable workflows, controls, and escalation procedures. Experience coordinating across distributed teams, third parties, and multiple levels of technical and business support. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Business Analyst, Associate – BTO
jobs.jd: About this role Your team The BlackRock Transformation Office (BTO) is a global group of change professionals that delivers strategic transformation to help make BlackRock greater than the sum of its parts. We drive 1BLK outcomes by continuously connecting and being students of the firm’s people, processes and technology. We are a versatile team with varied experiences and backgrounds, motivated by the challenge of finding solutions that benefit BlackRock and our clients. In BTO, we focus on developing our people, strengthening leadership and delivery skills, and broadening firm and industry knowledge. Projects and roles consider both successful delivery and individual development objectives and career aspirations. Your role and impact The Forward Deployed Business Analyst will work in cross-functional teams to reimagine, innovate and scale solutions that drive growth and operating models within the firm. This is not a traditional business analysis role centered on gathering requirements and handing them to technology. The role combines business analysis, product discovery, business architecture and hands-on prototyping to turn ambiguous problems into tangible solutions that business users and engineers can test and refine together. Successful candidates will combine the structured thinking of a business analyst, the prioritization instincts of a product owner, the enterprise perspective of a business architect and the bias to action of a hands-on builder. Your responsibilities In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities: Take ownership of complex, ambiguous business problems and rapidly translate them into testable solution hypotheses with measurable outcomes. Build structured business context covering terminology, entities, relationships, decision logic, data dependencies, controls and exceptions for use by subject matter experts, AI tools and engineering teams. Decompose business processes into explicit logic, controls and exception paths for implementation by technology teams. Create functional prototypes using AI-enabled development capabilities to discover requirements, challenge assumptions and validate future-state processes, data, policies and controls. Shape the target operating model, including ownership of data, governance, controls, roles and exception management. Partner continuously with business experts, product managers, engineers, architects, data specialists and control partners from discovery through implementation. Develop measurable project objectives, drive consensus, and communicate plans, progress and outcomes effectively to stakeholders and management across levels. Your experience 3–5 years of relevant work experience in transformation, product delivery, business architecture, technology-enabled change or a comparable discipline. Experience in business architecture and operating-model design, connecting solutions to business capabilities, roles, governance, policy ownership, controls and exception handling. Proficiency in prototype-led problem solving and rapidly converting ambiguous business problems into functional prototypes that stakeholders can see, test and challenge. Expertise using AI-enabled development environments to accelerate analysis, prototyping, requirements definition and testing, including critically evaluating generated outputs, maintaining traceability and understanding where human judgment remains essential. Experience with iterative delivery and hands-on ownership through cycles of analysis, experimentation and solution shaping. Experience in financial services or a similar industry. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate objectives and influence outcomes. Our benefits To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits including a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, comprehensive healthcare, support for working parents and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about. Our hybrid work model BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock. Guidance on AI use for candidates At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self. About BlackRock At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress. This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive. To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com . We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn , Instagram , YouTube , X , and TikTok . BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, family status, gender identity, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected attributes at law.

jobs.jd: Wood Mackenzie is the global leader in analytics, insights and proprietary data across the entire energy and natural resources landscape. Now, with the world’s energy system more complex and interconnected than ever before, sector-specific views are no longer enough. Our trusted team of 2,700 experts across 30 countries breaks siloes and connects industries, markets and regions across the globe. As a Power Market Analyst, you will play a key role in building, maintaining, and enhancing market optimization models used to analyse power systems, generation economics, transmission constraints, and market outcomes. You will apply linear programming (LP) and other optimization techniques to simulate market behaviour, assess investment and operational decisions, and provide actionable insights on power market dynamics, decarbonization pathways, and energy transition challenges. Key Responsibilities Develop, maintain, and enhance optimization-based power market models for European electricity markets. Design and implement LP and mixed-integer optimization models to simulate generation dispatch, storage operation, cross-border trading, and market-clearing mechanisms. Analyse power market fundamentals, including supply-demand dynamics, renewable integration, fuel markets, emissions costs, and transmission constraints. Conduct scenario analysis to evaluate market outcomes, asset profitability, policy impacts, and energy transition pathways. Translate complex model outputs into clear market insights and recommendations for internal stakeholders and clients. Improve model methodologies, assumptions, and analytical frameworks to enhance model accuracy, transparency, and performance. Work with large datasets and develop efficient data workflows to support model development and analysis. Collaborate with experts across power markets, renewable energy, economics, and policy to deliver high-quality research and market intelligence. Monitor developments in European energy markets, regulatory frameworks, and market design, assessing their impact on market participants and investment decisions. Support client engagements through presentations, bespoke analyses, technical discussions, and thought leadership. About You We are looking for a highly analytical and intellectually curious individual with a strong foundation in optimization, quantitative modelling, and power market analysis. You enjoy solving complex problems, building robust models, and generating insights that support strategic decision-making. Essential Skills and Qualifications A degree in Operations Research, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Economics, Energy Systems, Computer Science, or a related quantitative discipline. Experience in electricity market analysis, power system modeling, or energy economics. Strong knowledge of optimization techniques, particularly linear programming (LP) and mixed-integer programming (MIP). Experience developing and implementing mathematical models for power systems, generation portfolios, storage assets, or electricity markets. Proficiency in Python and/or other programming languages used for optimization and quantitative analysis. Experience with optimization frameworks and solvers such as Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, Pyomo, or similar tools. Strong understanding of European power market fundamentals, market design, and price formation mechanisms. Ability to analyze complex datasets and communicate technical findings clearly to both technical and commercial audiences. Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. Why Join Us? At Wood Mackenzie, you will work on industry-leading power market models that help clients navigate rapidly changing energy markets and the transition to a low-carbon economy. You will collaborate with leading analysts, modelers, and industry experts to solve complex challenges facing power systems, renewable integration, energy storage, and electricity market design. This role offers an opportunity to apply cutting-edge optimization techniques and market analysis to inform investment decisions, support policy evaluation, and shape the future of the energy sector. jobs.jd: We are pleased to announce the opening for a Missile Defense Architecture Analyst, who will join our Architecture Engineering team in Huntsville, Alabama. Qualified candidates will be part of an exceptional team supporting the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) mission to develop and deploy a layered Missile Defense System to defend the United States, its deployed forces, allies, and friends from missile attacks in all phases of flight. Responsibilities: The Missile Defense Architecture Analyst will be providing technical support to the Missile Defense Agency on the MDA Technical, Engineering, Advisory and Management Support. The unique, highly qualified SEA Team is critical to ensuring the MDA can rapidly develop and deploy missile defense capabilities to defeat advanced missile threats by aggressively pursuing advanced concepts and technologies for leap-ahead capability in directed energy, hypersonic missile defense, radiation hardened electronics, space-based sensors, and Israeli defense systems. The SEA Team provides comprehensive Missile Defense System test analyses, future Missile Defense System architecture modeling and design, advanced technology analyses, and specialized engineering support to improve the development, testing, and fielding of technical capabilities that are also cybersecure and tamper-proof. This position will support the office of the MDA Chief Architect and join a team developing and employing Benchmark, a performance modeling tool used for concept exploration and evaluation. This team increases the capability of the Missile Defense Agency to envision and define a future architecture that will enable our nation to stay ahead of adversary’s threat developments to ensure the safety of our nation and its allies globally. Duties include: Maintain awareness of performance assessments of the Missile Defense System at the full system level and among contributing weapon systems and update records on any present or future capability gaps that will drive future development efforts Contribute to architecture planning, requirements definition, and development activities at the enterprise level supporting strategic and regional architectures Develop analysis scripts using MATLAB and/or Python to build new capabilities within the Benchmark M&S environment to support trade study analyses for future concepts Conduct runs of the MDA Benchmark tool to perform predictive analysis about potential future missile defense architecture laydowns against theoretical/conceptual future threat environments Basic Qualifications: This position is open only to US Citizens. You must have 7+ years working on missile defense-related or other complex, large DoD program/project or industry equivalent. You must have a Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field such as engineering, physics, or math. Must possess excellent oral and written communication skills and critical thinking abilities. Must be capable of working independently and within teams to solve complex problems. You must possess or have the ability to obtain an active Secret clearance. Preferred Qualifications: Experience producing analysis tools using Matlab and/or Python or a similar scripting language. Familiarity with one or more elements of the Missile Defense System.

jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.jd: Job Description Summary As an entry-level Data Scientist, you will work with engineers, data professionals and product teams to frame problems, prepare data, build and evaluate analytical or machine-learning models, and communicate results. You will contribute to practical solutions that are technically rigorous, understandable and ready to be used by the business. This role is designed for a recent graduate who brings strong fundamentals, curiosity and evidence of applied project work. Job Description Key Responsibilities Partner with engineering and business stakeholders to translate a question into a clear analytical problem, success criteria and testable approach. Explore, clean, join and validate structured and unstructured datasets; document assumptions, limitations and data-quality issues. Build baseline and advanced models using statistical analysis, machine learning, optimization or time-series methods as appropriate. Compare models using relevant performance metrics and evaluate uncertainty, bias, robustness and generalization. Create clear visualizations, notebooks and concise presentations that explain methods, findings and recommended actions. Work with Data Engineers and AI Engineers to move useful analyses from prototypes toward reusable, monitored solutions. Use version control, code review, testing and reproducible workflows to create maintainable analytical assets. Protect confidential information and follow cybersecurity, data governance, intellectual property and Responsible AI requirements. Continue developing domain knowledge in energy, engineering and industrial systems through hands-on work and mentorship. Required Qualifications Recent graduate with a Bachelor's or Master's degree completed by the start date in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, Operations Research, Physics or a related quantitative field. 0-1 year of related experience in STEM Foundational knowledge of statistics, probability, experimental design and machine-learning concepts. Hands-on experience with Python or R through coursework, research, internships, co-ops or independent projects. Experience using common data analysis and visualization tools such as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, SQL, Jupyter, matplotlib, seaborn, Power BI or equivalents. jobs.title: Operations Specialist
jobs.jd: Kodiak AI, Inc. (Nasdaq: KDK), founded in 2018, is a leader in Physical AI, developing driverless technology that powers machines that move. Its Kodiak Driver is a vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving system that combines AI-powered software with modular hardware. Today it operates in long-haul trucking, industrial trucking, and defense. In 2024, Kodiak launched commercial Driver-as-a-Service operations with no one in the cab, and plans to launch driverless long-haul service between Dallas and Houston by the end of 2026. Kodiak has partnered with many of the biggest names in freight, including Bosch for scaled hardware production, AWS, and leading customers including Atlas Energy Solutions, IKEA, Bridgestone, Werner Enterprises, C.R. England, Roehl Transport, and General Dynamics Land Systems. jobs.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant, Bilingual - Mint Urban Infinity
jobs.jd: At Cortland, we operate with a forward-thinking approach that challenges conventional norms and actively seeks insights beyond traditional industry boundaries. As a recognized leader in the multifamily sector, our focus on performance, innovation, and disciplined execution continues to drive strong growth and market leadership. We are committed to building a best-in-class organization by empowering top talent with the resources, autonomy, and support needed to deliver results and advance their careers in a high-performance environment. Role Overview As a Bilingual Leasing & Sales Consultant, you’ll be the driving force behind occupancy and revenue at your community. This role goes beyond leasing apartments; it’s about selling a lifestyle and creating an experience that makes people proud to call Cortland “home.” You’ll combine proactive sales strategies with exceptional engagement to turn prospects into residents and keep your community thriving. Sales & Revenue Generation: Drive occupancy and revenue by achieving and exceeding leasing goals, conversion targets, and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Actively manage your sales pipeline—follow up promptly, nurture potential residents, and close leases with confidence. Use consultative selling techniques to uncover needs, present solutions, and create value that resonates with each potential resident. Keep CRM records accurate and up to date for all potential resident interactions. Monitor and report on lead activity, conversion metrics, and pipeline health. Stay organized and disciplined to ensure timely follow-up and consistent engagement. Community Advocacy & Resident Experience: Guide potential residents through the leasing process with confidence and care, making it simple, stress-free, and enjoyable journey that reinforces our brand promise of better living. Deliver a concierge-level experience by anticipating needs, offering personalized solutions, and creating memorable interactions. Build lasting relationships that inspire loyalty and referrals through exceptional service. Represent the community as an ambassador, showcasing not just homes but a lifestyle of comfort, convenience, and premium living. Handle objections gracefully, turning challenges into opportunities. Establish, manage, and maintain marketing programs and social media presence to attract and retain residents. Plan and execute resident events and engagement programs that strengthen community ties. Adaptability & Continuous Improvement: Respond to coaching and feedback with agility; implement best practices promptly. Adjust sales approach based on market conditions, prospect needs, and leadership guidance. Professionalism & Brand Alignment: Maintain integrity, accountability, and reliability in all aspects of performance. Maintain a polished, approachable presence that reflects our premium brand standards in every interaction. Qualifications 6+ months of sales, customer-facing, or performance-driven experience preferred. Strong desire to succeed in a goal-oriented, fast-paced sales environment. Confident, persuasive, and people-focused with a natural ability to build rapport. Coachable and resilient, with a positive attitude and willingness to learn. Motivated by targets, results, and earning potential; comfortable being held to goals. Organized and disciplined with follow-up, time management, and attention to detail. Comfortable learning and using CRM systems to track leads and customer interactions. Professional, polished, and approachable with a strong sense of personal presentation. Aligns with company values and takes pride in representing a premium brand experience. Recognized as one of the top 10 multifamily owners and operators in the US, Cortland combines in-house design, construction, and operations to deliver value and innovation across its portfolio. Join us as we reimagine apartment living and drive outsized returns through purpose, performance, and people.
