COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.




COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.



The Opportunity

Deepgram is hiring a Revenue Operations Analyst to help build and operate the systems, data, and workflows that power our GTM organization.

This is a hands-on role for someone who likes getting into the details: fixing broken workflows, improving data quality, supporting quote-to-cash and usage-based billing processes, and finding ways to automate repetitive work. You’ll work closely with GTM Engineering, Finance, Sales, Customer Success, and Renewals to make our commercial systems more reliable, scalable, and efficient.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Support and improve quote-to-cash workflows, including CPQ, order forms, contract changes, subscriptions, entitlements, and downstream system updates.

 - Partner with Finance and GTM Engineering on usage, billing, and monetization workflows, including reconciliation across CRM, product, billing, and finance systems.

 - Serve as a hands-on Salesforce and GTM systems operator, building reports, dashboards, flows, automations, and system enhancements.

 - Maintain strong data quality and governance across accounts, opportunities, contracts, usage, renewals, and customer records.

 - Troubleshoot and resolve GTM systems and process issues, identifying root causes rather than relying on manual workarounds.

 - Identify repetitive or high-friction workflows and help build automation and AI-enabled solutions to reduce manual effort.

 - Support the systems and reporting used to operationalize forecasting, routing, territory, quota, and commission decisions.

 - Partner with the Director, GTM Engineering on system requirements, testing, implementation, documentation, and ongoing optimization.

 - Help create scalable operating processes as Deepgram grows, while staying close to the day-to-day work that surfaces where systems need to improve.


IT’S IMPORTANT TO US THAT YOU HAVE

 - 3–4+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, GTM Systems, Sales Operations, Business Systems, or a related role.

 - Strong hands-on Salesforce experience, including reporting, flows, automation, and data management.

 - Experience working across CRM, CPQ, billing, contract, or other GTM systems.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.

 - A track record of improving workflows, not just executing existing processes.

 - Comfort using AI and automation tools to reduce manual work and improve operations.

 - Ability to work cross-functionally across GTM, Finance, and technical teams.


IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAD

 - Experience in a usage-based or consumption-based business.

 - Experience with CPQ and contract-generation tools.

 - Familiarity with billing or metering systems.

 - SQL or experience working with GTM/customer data.

 - Experience with tools such as Claude, Cursor, n8n, Workato, Retool, or similar automation environments.

 - Experience in a high-growth SaaS or AI company.

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com http://deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

 - Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment with evolving systems, processes, and priorities

jobs.title: Supply Chain Analyst
jobs.jd:
About the role

The owner of Pocket’s demand forecast, inventory health, and fulfillment planning. You answer three critical questions: how many units we’re going to sell, when we need to order them, and where the inventory needs to be.

Pocket sells physical products across DTC, Amazon, retail, and international markets. You’ll monitor demand, identify stock risks early, and coordinate with warehouses and fulfillment partners to keep products available without tying up unnecessary cash.

This is a hands-on role on a lean team. You’ll work with imperfect data, build processes where none exist, and directly influence availability, delivery speed, and shipping cost.

What you'll own

 - Daily demand monitoring and the weekly forecast across channels, SKUs, and colorways

 - Reorder points, safety stock, days of coverage, and purchase order recommendations

 - Stockout and overstock risk identification, with clear mitigation plans

 - Amazon FBA shipment planning and inventory health across marketplaces

 - Day-to-day execution with 3PL and fulfillment partners

 - Inventory placement across warehouses to balance availability, delivery speed, and cost

 - Reconciliation of inventory and fulfillment data across systems

 - The core numbers: forecast accuracy, in-stock rate, inventory turns, days of coverage, and fulfillment cost

What we're looking for

 - 1–3 years in supply chain, demand planning, inventory, or fulfillment operations for a physical product

 - You’ve built and maintained a real forecast and can explain where it was wrong

 - Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills and comfort working with messy data from multiple systems

 - Strong understanding of lead times, safety stock, reorder points, and MOQs

 - High attention to detail and ownership of the accuracy of your work

 - You chase answers, move quickly, and figure things out without detailed instructions

 - Experience with Amazon FBA, 3PLs, WMS/ERP systems, SQL, or high-growth ecommerce is a strong plus

What we offer

 - Direct impact on inventory and fulfillment at a fast-scaling YC company

 - High ownership and direct access to founders and the senior team

 - A lean, fast-moving environment with room to grow into broader supply chain ownership
   
   




About Pocket

Pocket is a Y Combinator W26 company building a premium hardware plus software product in the AI voice recorder space. We are obsessed with quality and speed. We are scaling very fast in the US and now European markets and building a device experience that can become the category leader.

jobs.title: Founding Growth Marketer, B2B
jobs.jd:
About the role

The first marketer on Pocket's B2B team. Most people use Pocket for work, and most of them bought it themselves. Companies ask for it for whole teams, usually because someone inside already uses it. Your job is to reach the ones that haven't asked yet. You figure out which channels bring in teams that buy - paid, content, SEO, lifecycle - then run them yourself and scale what works. You work closely with our D2C marketing team, who already run paid, creative and lifecycle at scale: take what works from them and ask when you're stuck. This is a hands-on generalist role: you build the pages, launch the campaigns, write the copy, brief the creative and read the numbers. We approach marketing like engineering: measure everything, test on purpose, automate what repeats.


What you'll own

 - The B2B website: team and pricing pages, landing pages for the professions that use Pocket most, and the path from visit to talk-to-sales

 - Paid acquisition for B2B: Meta, Google, LinkedIn, etc.

 - Content and SEO: finding what brings in business buyers and doing it, from guides to comparison pages

 - Proof: case studies, customer logos, review sites, and the third-party coverage buyers and AI search look for

 - Lifecycle: email and in-app campaigns that move people using Pocket at work toward a team plan

 - Creative: briefs, testing and a steady flow of new ads, made with our designer

 - Tracking and data: attribution, dashboards and experiments you set up yourself, cost per deal by channel, and what you change when it moves

What we're looking for

 - 3+ years in growth or performance marketing, at least part of it selling to businesses

 - Hands-on: you've run the paid campaigns, shipped the pages and written the copy yourself

 - You know when content or SEO will beat paid, and when it won't

 - You write clearly and fast: headlines, landing pages, emails

 - AI-native: LLMs, no-code tools and automations are how you work

 - Data-driven, with an engineering streak: SQL, tracking and attribution setup, dashboards you build yourself

 - Comfortable starting with no B2B playbook and making the calls yourself

Bonus points for:

 - Marketing hardware plus subscription

 - Turning individual users into team accounts

 - Webflow, HubSpot or similar tools, hands-on

 - Python or scripting to automate your own work

 - An engineering or analytics background

What we offer

 - The first marketing seat in a fast-growing B2B function

 - A path to leading B2B marketing as it scales

 - An experienced D2C marketing team to work with and learn from

 - Direct impact on how the company grows

 - A high-trust, high-responsibility environment with direct founder access

 - Competitive compensation and equity

About Pocket

Pocket is a Y Combinator W26 company building a premium hardware plus software product in the AI voice recorder space. We are obsessed with quality and speed. We are scaling very fast in the US and now European markets and building a device experience that can become the category leader.

jobs.title: Payments & Commercial Abuse Analyst
jobs.jd: The Payments & Commercial Abuse Analyst identifies, investigates, and mitigates fraud, abuse, and monetization risks across Adobe's commerce ecosystem. Through data-driven investigations, payment risk analysis, abuse detection, and cross-functional partnerships, the team uncovers emerging threats, develops scalable mitigations, and delivers actionable intelligence that protects revenue, reduces customer friction, and strengthens trust in Adobe products and services. Key Responsibilities & Areas of Impact - The responsibilities below represent the primary areas of focus for this role and may evolve alongside emerging risks, business priorities, and organizational needs. Payments Risk & Commercial Abuse Investigations Investigate complex payment fraud, monetization abuse, account misuse, and commercial abuse schemes impacting Adobe's commerce ecosystem , including unauthorized resale activity, synthetic identity abuse, payment instrument abuse, chargeback fraud, refund abuse, and the unauthorized use, distribution, or commercialization of Adobe products and services. Analyze transactions, customer behaviors, payment activity, subscription usage, account relationships, and associated signals to identify suspicious patterns, assess risk exposure, determine root cause, and recommend mitigation, enforcement, or policy actions. Evaluate escalations, emerging threat patterns, and high-risk activity to develop risk assessments and response recommendations. Analytics, Intelligence & Detection Development Utilize SQL, analytical tools, and investigative methodologies to identify trends, uncover fraud patterns, validate hypotheses, and generate actionable intelligence. Translate investigative findings into scalable detection strategies, risk signals, decisioning logic, and operational controls that reduce fraud while minimizing friction for legitimate customers. Partner with Data Science, Engineering, and AI teams to define abuse indicators, improve model performance, and enhance detection capabilities through investigator-driven insights and feedback loops. Produce intelligence assessments, trend analyses, and strategic insights on emerging abuse patterns, monetization risks, and evolving fraud trends across Adobe's commerce ecosystem. Commerce Risk Strategy & Optimization Balance fraud prevention objectives with customer experience considerations when evaluating controls, policies, detection strategies, and enforcement actions. Provide recommendations to strengthen payment risk controls, fraud mitigation strategies, automation opportunities, and long-term commerce risk initiatives while balancing customer experience and business objectives. Collaborate with Product, Commerce, Risk, Customer Support, Trust & Safety, and Engineering teams to address emerging threats, improve platform resilience, and drive sustainable risk reduction strategies. Qualifications & Core Competencies : Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex investigative findings, payment risk data, and abuse trends into clear, actionable recommendations. Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to identify patterns, assess risk, and transform complex data into meaningful insights that drive informed decision-making. Experience using SQL /SPL and data analysis techniques to support investigations, validate hypotheses, identify trends, and generate actionable intelligence. A naturally inquisitive and investigative mindset, with a passion for understanding how malicious actors exploit commerce systems, products, and business processes. Strong understanding of payment and commerce risk concepts, including chargebacks, friendly fraud, account abuse, refund abuse, affiliate abuse, subscription fraud, identity risk, monetization abuse, and common payment ecosystem risks. Experience identifying risk signals, anomalous behaviors, and abuse patterns and translating findings into scalable detection, mitigation, or enforcement strategies. Creative and strategic problem-solving capabilities, including the ability to anticipate emerging risks and develop innovative, scalable solutions. Proven ability to manage competing priorities and adapt quickly in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. Self-motivated, proactive, and comfortable operating with ambiguity while working independently and collaboratively across cross-functional teams. Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and commitment to delivering thorough, accurate, and high-confidence investigative outcomes. Experience in payments risk, commerce fraud, fraud investigations, abuse prevention, trust and safety operations, fraud analytics, cybersecurity investigations, threat intelligence, or enterprise risk management is preferred. Familiarity with machine learning concepts, risk models, AI-driven abuse trends, or the application of AI and automation to fraud detection and investigative workflows is a plus. Ability to balance fraud prevention objectives with customer experience, operational efficiency, and business outcomes when evaluating risk mitigation strategies. jobs.title: Analyste Financier
jobs.jd: C'est votre chance de rejoindre une organisation en évolution rapide avec une présence importante, stable et en croissance constante dans l'industrie du logiciel! jobs.jd: At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. Finance Analyst – Expedia Controllership Position Description The Expedia Business to Business Controllership team is seeking a Finance Analyst to supervise and report on the direct billing and cash settlement processes for B2B partnerships which is a growing and innovative business. You will report to the Finance Manager of B2B Controllership and closely partner with Account Management, Accounting, Corporate Accounts Payable/Receivable, Tax, Treasury, and Technology teams. You will prepare contractual results supporting processes for strategic B2B partners and gain a deep understanding of the product and insight into the end-to-end business process. This position is part of the B2B team, located in Springfield, MO, and is responsible for supporting receivables and payables processes, partner requests, user acceptance testing, and process improvement initiatives for B2B Loyalty Points partners. Responsibilities include supporting month-end close activities, coordinating AR/AP processes, assisting with daily communications with partners and internal stakeholders, and contributing to the continued growth and evolution of the Loyalty Points operations business. Key Areas of Responsibility · Support partner requirements for billing, cash receipts, cash settlements, automated reporting, and reconciliations. · Prepare, distribute, and maintain the daily aging report for the EPS Loyalty portfolio, with partial ownership of reporting accuracy, remediation tracking, and aging-related business insights. · Prepare monthly AR snapshot reports and support analysis of receivable trends. · Assist with month-end close activities, including AR and AP reconciliations, accrual support, account analysis, and other close-related responsibilities. · Support the execution and monitoring of accounts receivable and accounts payable processes to ensure accurate and timely financial reporting. · Assist with new partner intake, including setup for billing, cash settlement, and daily/monthly reporting packages. · Partner with multiple teams to continuously monitor and evaluate the quality of financial outputs and proactively drive process improvements. · Support the ongoing automation, enhancement, and operational development of the EPS Loyalty Points business, collaborating closely with Oracle, Product, Technology, Commercial, and Accounting teams. · Support ongoing process improvements for the points burn process and related settlement activities, helping identify scalable solutions as the business grows. · Participate in user acceptance testing (UAT) for system enhancements and new partner implementations. · Manage partner inquiries and collaborate with account managers and internal stakeholders to resolve billing and settlement issues. · Support ad hoc analyses, reporting requests, and strategic initiatives across EPS Enterprise Solutions. Requirements | Qualifications · Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent experience with demonstrated knowledge of accounting, financial analysis, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and month-end close processes. 2+ years of professional Finance or Accounting experience. · Basic understanding of accounting principles, including accounts receivable, accounts payable, reconciliations, accruals, and month-end close processes. · Intermediate Excel and PowerPoint skills. · Proven ability to manage multiple competing priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. · Adaptable and energized by change while maintaining focus on key business goals and objectives. · Strong quantitative and analytical skills with the ability to transform raw data into meaningful business insights. · Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate financial reporting and process execution. · Experience with Oracle, Business Objects, Tableau, or similar financial reporting tools is a plus. Employees in this role have the potential to increase their pay up to $88,000.00, which is the top of the range, based on ongoing, demonstrated, and sustained performance in the role. jobs.title: UX Design Operations Coordinator
jobs.jd: About Arlo: At Arlo, we're passionate about creating innovative and reliable solutions that help people protect what matters most to them. Our team is dedicated to delivering products that exceed our customers' expectations, while always pushing the boundaries of what's possible in the world of protection technology. We believe that everyone deserves to feel safe and secure, whether they're at home or away, and we're committed to providing our customers with the peace of mind they need to live their lives without worry. Arlo’s deep expertise in AI- and CV-powered analytics, cloud services, user experience, product design, and innovative wireless and RF connectivity enables the delivery of a seamless, smart security experience for Arlo users that is easy to set up and interact with every day. About the role The UX Design Operations Coordinator is a six-month contract role supporting Arlo's User Experience organization. This role helps the UX team operate efficiently and maintain clear visibility across a portfolio of software, hardware, and service experiences. The coordinator will partner closely with Design leadership, designers, Product Management, Engineering, Program Management, and other business partners to keep priorities, resources, timelines, dependencies, decisions, and deliverables aligned. This is a highly collaborative, detail-oriented role for someone who enjoys bringing structure to complex work, improving team processes, and keeping projects moving. The role is focused on operational excellence rather than visual design execution. What you'll be doing · Partner with UX Design leadership to coordinate the team's project portfolio, priorities, capacity, and key deliverables across mobile, web, hardware, and platform experiences. · Maintain project plans, schedules, milestones, status, dependencies, risks, and action items; proactively surface issues that could affect delivery. · Coordinate design resourcing across projects and help leadership identify capacity gaps, competing priorities, and opportunities to rebalance work. · Provide clear, concise project and portfolio visibility for stakeholders, including regular updates on priorities, resource utilization, milestones, risks, and decisions. · Act as an operational bridge between Design, Product Management, Engineering, Program Management, and other cross-functional partners to ensure dependencies and handoffs are understood and managed. · Own or facilitate the UX design intake process, helping teams capture requests, clarify scope and timing, assess priority, and route work appropriately. · Identify opportunities to improve UX workflows, tools, documentation, asset management, and team rituals; help implement practical changes that increase efficiency and reduce friction. · Coordinate key design reviews, planning sessions, workshops, and leadership meetings, including agendas, materials, action items, and follow-through. · Connect related work across products, features, platforms, and initiatives; identify potential collisions, duplicated effort, or gaps and work with partners to resolve them. · Support quarterly and annual planning by consolidating project commitments, resource needs, timelines, and operational risks into a clear view for UX leadership and business partners. · Help maintain operational systems and reporting used by the UX organization, including project trackers, planning tools, documentation, and shared team resources. · Bring together business goals, customer needs, technology, design intent, and execution realities so teams can make informed decisions and keep work progressing. What you should have · Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience. · Experience in design operations, design program management, project management, agency operations, or a closely related role. · Experience working with creative or UX teams and an understanding of how to introduce useful process and structure without slowing creative work. · Strong project management skills, including the ability to organize complex programs, prioritize competing needs, manage schedules, and follow through independently. · Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across Design, Product, Engineering, and business teams. · Strong attention to detail and comfort managing multiple workstreams, dependencies, and deadlines at the same time. · Experience with project tracking, planning, documentation, and collaboration tools; familiarity with tools such as Smartsheet, Jira, Confluence, Figma, or similar platforms is a plus. · Experience working in an Agile product development environment. · Ability to create clear status reports, presentations, trackers, and other operational materials for a range of audiences, including senior leadership. · Understanding of UX design and product development processes; familiarity with qualitative and quantitative user research is a plus. · Experience supporting hardware + software or connected-device products is a plus, particularly mobile, web, IoT, or smart-home experiences. · Comfort working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can evolve and ambiguity needs to be turned into action. Contract scope This is a six-month contract position designed to provide experienced operational support to the UX Design organization. The successful candidate will be expected to quickly establish relationships, understand existing workflows and priorities, and provide immediate structure and continuity across the team's active portfolio. What success looks like · UX leadership has a clear, current view of project priorities, resourcing, milestones, and risks. · Cross-functional partners understand ownership, dependencies, timing, and next steps. · Design requests are captured, prioritized, and routed through a consistent process. · Project and team operations are organized, documented, and easy to navigate. · The UX team spends less time on operational friction and more time focused on delivering high-quality customer experiences. We’re committed to inclusivity and selecting the strongest candidate—no matter their background. Even if you don’t meet every listed qualification, we encourage you to apply. We’re happy to support growth in areas essential to the role. Interested in learning more about our workplace? Visit and follow our LinkedIn , and Glassdoor pages to read employee insights and get updates of what it’s like to be part of Arlo. Arlo is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value inclusion and are committed to inclusive, and harassment-free workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment based on all legally protected statuses in all hiring and employment. We provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities, who are pregnant or have a related medical condition, or who have sincerely held religious beliefs, observances, and practices. Pursuant to applicable state and municipal Fair Chance Laws and Ordinances, the Company will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.jd: Job Description: This position will support the Research, Science and Engineering Services (RSES) contract onsite at NASA Langley Research Center in Hampton, VA. Job Descriptions: The qualified candidates will be responsible for providing the Government with structural mechanics, dynamics, and thermal analysis, along with work products for detailed structural systems supporting flight missions, conceptual designs, and exploration projects. This includes Earth, lunar, and planetary exploration. These engineering work products will encompass detailed analysis of the following. Responsibilities: Perform System-level structural and thermal analysis supporting flight, ground, and test hardware design and development Perform Finite Element modeling/analysis element modeling/analysis in environments ranging from earth & other planetary atmospheres Perform static/dynamic loads and stress analyses of complex aerospace systems Develop reports, presentations and other documentation Generate assembly/integration and test procedures Knowledge of acceptance standards for spaceflight hardware applications Attend meetings and teleconferences and be ready to discuss issues seen in design, analysis, qualification and acceptance plans and reports Required Qualifications: A bachelor’s degree in Structural, Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering from an accredited university. Demonstrated use of Patran, FEMAP, or similar software, solve using NX or MSC Nastran, document the analysis, present/report findings, guide design and manufacturing, and verify results using testing. Models may vary from Ground Support Equipment (GSE) or test fixturing to electronic boxes, flight science instruments, flight vehicles or satellites. Demonstrated experience documenting reports, and technical memos in both Microsoft Word and PowerPoint and presenting findings to internal NASA groups, designers, project leadership, and customers at project meetings, branch meetings, and design reviews as requested by project managers. Experience with Python programming or similar. Familiarity with the Microsoft Office suite of tools. US citizenship is required or Permanent Residence. Desired Experience: Experience in performing Structural, Thermal and Optical Performance (STOP) analysis Experience with Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and/or MBSE Multidisciplinary Design Analysis and Optimization (MDAO) or optimization and/or sensitivity studies scripting models together for system-based analyses. Models are often made from scratch or by using CAD geometry as a framework, a Working knowledge of PTC/CREO software is also highly desired. Knowledge of advanced structural techniques such as nonlinear material behavior, fatigue, fracture, or optimization will also be considered. jobs.title: Financial Analyst I
jobs.jd: By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive. Financial Administration (FAD) is dedicated to advancing Harvard University’s teaching and research mission by stewarding its resources; providing support, guidance, and consultation; ensuring compliance with university and federal guidelines; mitigating risk; pursuing operational excellence; and promoting the financial health of the University. More about FAD: Within and across the University, we aim to be exemplary colleagues, trusted partners, valued advisors, and agents of positive change. Within our own community, we aspire to: Engage with respect, honesty, and integrity Cultivate equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging Welcome innovation, collaboration, and flexibility Enjoy our work, grow professionally, and aim for the extraordinary Learn more about Financial Administration (harvard.edu) and our eight reporting units. ( https://finance.harvard.edu/) The Office for Sponsored Programs is a department within Harvard University’s Financial Administration (FAD) that is focused on providing high-quality administrative and financial assistance to faculty and other University affiliates performing sponsored research. OSP works with researchers and schools across Harvard to help obtain and negotiate awards from sponsoring agencies, assist with grant proposal preparation, ensure compliance with federal regulations and University policies, provide financial support including financial reporting and billing and collection services, assist with audits, and promote knowledge of sponsored research administration throughout the University research community through training and other educational programs. The Financial Analyst I (FA I) supports the Research Finance Operations (RFO) Team in the Office for Sponsored Programs (OSP). The three core functions of this role are: Apply standard practices with the interpretation and recording of financial terms in the Grants Management Application Suite (GMAS) Prepare and submit a high volume of standardized invoices and reports to sponsors Monitor and facilitate the collection of outstanding accounts receivable. This role requires the ability to balance accuracy with working in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment. The FA I is responsible for reviewing sponsored agreements for any terms related to payment and financial reporting and for setting up the schedule of invoices, financial reports (financial deliverables), and other related data in GMAS. The FA I is also responsible for completing standard invoices and standard financial reports as assigned each month using an automated process in GMAS. In doing so, the FA I may be required to work directly with sponsors, clients, and colleagues to ensure the sponsor requirements are met. The FA I also performs the accounts receivable collection of any outstanding sponsored payments and coordinates collections efforts with sponsors and clients when necessary. Approximately 35% effort is anticipated for scheduling, 35% for invoicing and financial reporting, 20% for accounts receivable collection, and 10% for project-based duties, which can include business process documentation, training initiatives, account reconciliation and closeout, ad hoc data analysis, and other special projects. Job-Specific Responsibilities: Serves as a principal source of information for interpreting complex financial terms and conditions within sponsored agreements Accurately records financial deliverable schedules and related information in the sponsored system of record (GMAS) Produces timely and accurate invoices and financial reports based on sponsor deadlines Analyzes financial data to identify potential risks and issues (quantitatively and qualitatively) in a way that is meaningful and proposes solutions for complex issues and best practices, which may require the entry of adjustments in the General Ledger Works within the team and across Research Finance to update and develop business processes and identify best practices Liaise effectively with other groups, such as sponsors, school financial offices, academic department leadership, pre-award offices, and central finance and technology units to clarify sponsor requirements, business processes, and systems Provides backfill support for peers or additional support during busy periods, when required, consistently applying processes and practices to new assignments Assists with developing and delivering metrics/reports, business process documentation, training initiatives, and special projects as needed Basic Qualifications: Basic Qualifications are the minimum threshold a candidate must meet in order to be considered for this role. For consideration, please include a cover letter. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience required 3+ years of direct accounting, financial management, data analysis, and/or grants management experience. Progress toward relevant professional certification may count toward experience. Additional Qualifications and Skills: The following qualifications are strongly preferred. If you meet some, but not all, you are still encouraged to apply; we value employees with a willingness to learn. Ability to prioritize and handle large volumes of work in a deadline driven environment Ability to work independently and as part of a team Strong attention to detail with excellent organizational and time management skills Ability to handle complex and confidential information with discretion and judgment Working knowledge of accounting and direct experience in financial management Experience with fund accounting or sponsored accounting Experience in sponsored programs or a research environment Problem-solving orientation and ability to be thorough and detail-oriented, but also able to summarize and convey the bigger picture Proven ability to utilize multiple financial and reporting systems, as well as other applications (i.e. Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Adobe) Demonstrated strength in written and verbal communication Why join Harvard University Central Administration? Harvard University's Central Administration (CADM) is a 5,000+ employee organization that supports the university's overall excellence by understanding and serving the needs of its schools, students, faculty, staff, alumni, and surrounding communities. Through dynamic and collaborative partnerships, CADM provides high-quality and efficient services to the schools to help them achieve their goals. Working Conditions: Primarily remote role with flexibility to work on-site and optional in-person meetings bi-monthly. On-site attendance expectations may evolve based on business needs. Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Education Other Information: This position has a 90-day orientation and review period. Work Format Details This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that some of the duties and responsibilities can be effectively performed at a non-Harvard location. The work schedule and location will be set by the department at its discretion and based upon operational needs. When not working at a Harvard or Harvard-designated location, employees in hybrid positions must work in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts . Additional details will be discussed during the interview process. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment. Salary Grade and Ranges This position is salary grade level 055. Please visit Harvard's Salary Ranges to vi

jobs.jd: By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. Chan School of Public Health seeks a research assistant II non-lab to work with Professor Aisha Yousafzai, Professor of Child Development and Health. We are seeking an organized, detail-oriented, and proactive Operations Coordinator to provide daily administrative and operational support to the Pennsylvania Distribution Center (PADC). jobs.title: Technical Business Systems Analyst
jobs.jd: CapTech is an award-winning consulting firm that collaborates with clients to achieve what’s possible through the power of technology. At CapTech, we’re passionate about the work we do and the results we achieve for our clients. From the outset, our founders shared a collective passion to create a consultancy centered on strong relationships that would stand the test of time. Today we work alongside clients that include Fortune 100 companies, mid-sized enterprises, and government agencies, a list that spans across the country. Technical Business Systems Analysts (BSAs) at CapTech work side-by-side with business and technical stakeholders to define complex solutions, drive solution design, and ensure delivered products meet real business needs. Our BSAs work on a wide range of initiatives—from custom digital product development to large-scale integration, modernization, and enterprise transformation efforts spanning multiple systems, technologies, and lines of business. This Technical BSA role is ideal for someone who enjoys operating at the intersection of business and technology, thrives in ambiguity, and brings a consultant’s mindset to problem solving. Successful candidates are comfortable translating business objectives into technical requirements, partnering closely with architects and engineers, and helping teams navigate complex systems, integrations, and data challenges. You will play a hands-on role throughout the full delivery lifecycle, helping teams move from unclear problems to well-designed, scalable, and maintainable solutions. Quickly become familiar with client business challenges, processes, and technology landscapes in order to act as a trusted advisor and subject-matter partner to stakeholders. Act as a key contributor on cross-functional teams through all phases of the system delivery lifecycle, from discovery through delivery and validation. Support requirements elicitation using interviews, workshops, and collaborative working sessions to surface business needs and clarify solution intent. Translate business objectives into detailed functional and technical requirements that guide architecture, development, testing, and deployment activities. Partner with architects, engineers, and product teams to support solution design, including data modeling, API and integration requirements, interface definitions, and system workflows. Analyze data to understand current-state structures, data quality, and business impact, and help define how data supports future-state solutions. Support complex system integrations by documenting data mappings, business rules, system interactions, and upstream/downstream dependencies. Bridge business and technical perspectives to ensure solutions are valuable, usable, scalable, and maintainable. Evaluate current-state processes and systems, work with stakeholders to define a desired future state, and perform gap analysis to identify solution options and recommendations. Write and refine epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and backlog items as part of an Agile delivery team. Coordinate and support integration testing, system testing, and user acceptance testing (UAT) activities, including requirements traceability and validation. Identify risks, dependencies, assumptions, and impacts across business processes, systems, and integrations. Communicate clearly and effectively with technical teams, business stakeholders, and executive leadership, adapting your message to your audience. This role should expect a hybrid client-site schedule, with regular onsite visits each week based on engagement requirements. Required Qualifications: 3-10+ years of experience working as a Business Systems Analyst, Technical Architect, or similar role working on IT related initiatives and enterprise-scale solution delivery efforts. Prior consulting experience or demonstrated ability to operate effectively in a client-facing, advisory role. Demonstrated experience working on multi-system implementations, enterprise applications, and complex integrations. Experience partnering with software development teams throughout the full software delivery lifecycle. Experience creating process flows, data flows, sequence diagrams, system context diagrams, or other visual models that communicate business and technical solutions. Experience defining business rules, writing user stories, developing acceptance criteria, and managing requirements in Agile environments. Strong understanding of enterprise integration patterns, APIs, data flows, and modern cloud-based architectures. Ability to write and execute SQL queries to support analysis, troubleshooting, validation, and testing efforts. Experience performing data analysis, data mapping, and requirements traceability across multiple systems. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Proficiency with common delivery and collaboration tools such as JIRA, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or similar platforms. Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Preferred Qualifications: Experience supporting digital product development and product-centric delivery models. Experience working in regulated industries such as energy, utilities, infrastructure, financial services, healthcare, or public sector environments. Knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Salesforce, or other enterprise business platforms. Experience supporting cloud modernization, application modernization, or enterprise transformation initiatives. Familiarity with system architecture concepts, object-oriented design principles, or software engineering practices. Microsoft Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Scrum, Product Owner, CBAP, PMI-PBA, or related certifications. We provide challenging and impactful opportunities in our client work and internal teams, while keeping individual interests in mind. We want everyone at CapTech to be able to envision a lifelong career here, which is why we offer a variety of career paths based on your skills and passions. As a CapTecher, you will experience exciting and rewarding roles that help you grow and make a difference, while having fun along the way. At CapTech we offer a competitive and comprehensive benefits package including, but not limited to: CapTech is committed to providing a flexible work environment and helping our employees achieve a work-life balance that suits their individual needs. Employees must be available to work onsite in a client location or a CapTech office as requested. We allow CapTech employees to work remotely when compatible with CapTech and client needs. Competitive salary with performance-based bonus opportunities Three comprehensive Medical Plan options (PPO and HDHP), as well as Dental and Vision coverage Company paid basic Life and AD&D, Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Insurance Matching 401(k) Cell Phone stipend Competitive Paid Time Off Paid Birth and Family Bonding Leave Adoption Assistance Training and Certification opportunities eligible for expense reimbursement Team building and social activities Mentor program to help you develop your career CapTech is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a culture of equality, inclusion and fairness — each foundational to our core values. We strive to create a diverse environment where each employee is encouraged to bring their unique ideas, backgrounds and experiences to the workplace. At Aquatic, we are actively recruiting for a Financial Analyst to join our Finance team in Chicago. jobs.title: Fellow, Election Analytics
jobs.jd: The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as an elections analyst in New York. As an elections analytics fellow, you will contribute to The Times’s data-driven coverage of American elections. You will be part of the Election Analytics team, which produces The New York Times/Siena University Poll, the live election-night forecast known as The Needle and our polling tracker, in addition to stories that explore voter decisions and analyze past elections. Election Analytics is an interdisciplinary team of reporters, editors, developers and statisticians. You should have experience working in one of these areas and be excited to learn about the others. You will use your knowledge of elections and voting to contribute to stories, graphics and our longer-term projects. The exact form of this role will depend on your background. Perhaps you are more comfortable writing than coding and want to deepen your technical skills to more easily answer questions yourself. Or perhaps you bring a background as a developer or statistician and want to work on your ability to communicate your ideas in words. This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed. Responsibilities: Contribute original analyses of polls, voter registration trends and recent election results for articles or graphics Increase the team’s understanding of elections through data collection, scraping, statistical analysis and reporting Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world Basic Qualifications: No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships A deep and demonstrated understanding of American elections Experience working with data Expertise in at least one of the team’s focus areas: Data-driven reporting, including reporting clips or blog posts that demonstrate analytical findings meant for a broad audience Statistics, including experience developing statistical models in R or Python Development, including proficiency in R or Python, experience working with cloud computing providers and experience building productionized web applications Preferred Qualifications : Experience writing news stories, such as for a college newspaper To apply, upload a résumé, cover letter and an essay of no more than 500 words on a trend in American politics that you are watching. jobs.title: Supervisor, Safety Operations (Child Safety)
jobs.jd: SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars. SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next. SUPERVISOR, SAFETY OPERATIONS (CHILD SAFETY) SpaceXSI’s Safety team protects free expression while ensuring our users can safely and successfully engage with our platform through robust policy enforcement. Child Safety is our highest-stakes area: the team identifies, investigates, and removes child safety related abuse across X, Grok and X Money products, including AI-generated content, and makes the legally required reports to NCMEC. As we increasingly leverage AI-based automation, we innovate and experiment at a fast pace, striving to be a learning organization with a growth mindset. As Supervisor, Child Safety, you will lead the Austin-based Child Safety analyst team across shifts. You will be hands-on with escalations, improve the team quality and defensibility of every high-risk decision, and coordinate with Safety leadership, Legal, and law enforcement response teams on high-profile cases. You will lead the team’s shift from scaled manual review to analysts focused on “Automation First” appeals, model evaluations and audits, investigations, and escalations. RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead the Austin-based Child Safety team, a team of analysts (including senior analysts) covering X, Grok and X Money, with consistent standards across all shifts and strict adherence to SLAs Act as the escalation layer for Child Safety: be hands-on with complex, urgent, and high-profile cases, including high profile accounts, internal escalations from law enforcement response and legal teams, and SpacexSI products incident escalations Own NCMEC reporting decisions for the team. Ensure every enforcement decision is accurate, well-documented, and meets legal obligations, Bring thoughtful, well-reasoned recommendations to leadership on escalations, balancing the protection of minors with SpaceXSI’s free speech principles Run the team’s response to viral incidents and emerging abuse trends: track results, and escalate patterns quickly Take an automation-first approach. Partner with Program Leads to calibrate classifiers and turn findings into concrete improvements Lead the team’s automation evaluations, audits, and labeling ensuring high-quality curated data Use querying languages (e.g., SQL or Python) and LLM-powered agents to analyze operational data, identify trends, and drive data-informed improvements to policies and processes. Build that habit across the team Own your dashboards and KPIs: know hour to hour how the backlog and escalation queues are doing, and keep a baseline to spot and investigate anomalies Keep shift handovers, operational process documentation, and team performance trackers current so every analyst works from the same playbook Provide coaching, mentorship, and professional development to foster critical thinking, efficiency, growth, retention, and wellbeing in a team regularly exposed to highly sensitive content Run strong feedback loops as a proactive manager: give constructive feedback early and often, out of a desire to improve, and take it in stride Build the team into child safety subject matter experts with a defensibility mindset, so every decision can be explained and defended Own team performance end to end: set clear expectations, measure them, reward strong performers, and act quickly and fairly on underperformance Partner with internal stakeholders (e.g., HR, workforce management, Legal, Policy, other Safety teams) to align on Child Safety objectives and coverage All other duties and responsibilities as required by business need BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 5+ years of experience in online child safety, Trust & Safety operations, criminal investigations, or another safety field 2+ years of experience leading or supervising a team PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: Proven expertise in identifying and investigating CSAM, CSE and non-CSE related child safety areas, including grooming behaviors and risks in AI-generated content, with strong knowledge of legal obligations (such as NCMEC reporting) and industry standards for protecting minors Skilled in crisis and escalation management, with the ability to make sound, defensible decisions under pressure and navigate ambiguity in time-sensitive, high-impact situations Able to apply SpaceXSI safety policies with judgment, weighing the protection of minors against free expression in the global public square Proficient in data analysis with hands-on experience using LLMs, SQL, or Python to extract insights, identify emerging abuse vectors, and optimize operational performance Passionate about AI and automation, with an interest in leveraging technology to improve Child Safety enforcement and reduce manual workloads A strong communicator who can articulate business needs, write clear escalation summaries, and build relationships with Legal, Policy, Engineering, and leadership An active X - including Grok - user with a deep understanding of the platform’s role as a global public square and its Safety challenges A lifelong learner who reflects on their gaps, strives to fill them, and is curious about how to improve A team player who places the interests of the team first and balances mission accomplishment with compassion for their people Experience managing Child Safety or Trust & Safety teams at a social media or generative AI company, leveraging AI or other automation tools Expertise in leading red-teaming and adversarial testing of Large Language Models to proactively identify novel abuse vectors, jailbreaks, and safety failure modes, with a proven ability to translate findings into concrete improvements for enforcement systems, team processes, and platform robustness Experience providing human oversight and insights for scaled agentic AI operations, with abilities in prompting and evaluating LLM agents ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: This role will be on-site at our Austin, TX office, and might require off-shift support, including weekends as business needs arise This role may involve exposure to sensitive or graphic content, including vulgar language, violent threats, pornography, and other graphic images Must be willing to travel occasionally to collaborate with global teams SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice .

jobs.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant-Cortland Mirror Lake
jobs.jd: At Cortland, we operate with a forward-thinking approach that challenges conventional norms and actively seeks insights beyond traditional industry boundaries. As a recognized leader in the multifamily sector, our focus on performance, innovation, and disciplined execution continues to drive strong growth and market leadership. We are committed to building a best-in-class organization by empowering top talent with the resources, autonomy, and support needed to deliver results and advance their careers in a high-performance environment. Role Overview As a Leasing & Sales Consultant, you’ll be the driving force behind occupancy and revenue at your community. This role goes beyond leasing apartments; it’s about selling a lifestyle and creating an experience that makes people proud to call Cortland “home.” You’ll combine proactive sales strategies with exceptional engagement to turn prospects into residents and keep your community thriving. Sales & Revenue Generation: Drive occupancy and revenue by achieving and exceeding leasing goals, conversion targets, and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Actively manage your sales pipeline—follow up promptly, nurture potential residents, and close leases with confidence. Use consultative selling techniques to uncover needs, present solutions, and create value that resonates with each potential resident. Keep CRM records accurate and up to date for all potential resident interactions. Monitor and report on lead activity, conversion metrics, and pipeline health. Deliver a concierge-level experience by anticipating needs, offering personalized solutions, and creating memorable interactions. Build lasting relationships that inspire loyalty and referrals through exceptional service. Represent the community as an ambassador, showcasing not just homes but a lifestyle of comfort, convenience, and premium living. Handle objections gracefully, turning challenges into opportunities. Establish, manage, and maintain marketing programs and social media presence to attract and retain residents. Plan and execute resident events and engagement programs that strengthen community ties. Adaptability & Continuous Improvement: Respond to coaching and feedback with agility; implement best practices promptly. Adjust sales approach based on market conditions, prospect needs, and leadership guidance. Professionalism & Brand Alignment: Maintain integrity, accountability, and reliability in all aspects of performance. Maintain a polished, approachable presence that reflects our premium brand standards in every interaction. Qualifications 6+ months of sales, customer-facing, or performance-driven experience preferred. Strong desire to succeed in a goal-oriented, fast-paced sales environment. Confident, persuasive, and people-focused with a natural ability to build rapport. Coachable and resilient, with a positive attitude and willingness to learn. Motivated by targets, results, and earning potential; comfortable being held to goals. Organized and disciplined with follow-up, time management, and attention to detail. jobs.title: HR Workday Transformation Consultant
jobs.jd: Harbor is seeking a HR Workday Transformation Consultant to advise US clients on HR transformation and Workday, helping them plan, select and deliver change that lasts. Our HR and Payroll Transformation practice is growing quickly in the US, and this role is central to that growth. We advise organizations on how to modernize their HR and payroll functions, from the early business case through to system selection, implementation oversight and post go live support. Much of our work is with professional services firms, particularly large law firms, where we have built a strong reputation for independent, practical advice on Workday. Our US client base has grown rapidly over the past two years. We now need an experienced consultant on the ground who can lead client conversations, shape engagements and help us win new work. This is a remote position that can be worked from anywhere in the US, with preference given to those candidates located in the Eastern Time Zone near a major metropolitan area. Responsibilities: The role splits broadly into five areas, with the balance shifting depending on the client work in hand. HR Transformation Advisory Lead discovery and current state reviews of HR, payroll and people processes, and set out clear, costed options for change. Build business cases for HR technology investment, including benefits, costs, risks and timelines. Design target operating models for HR and HRIS teams, covering roles, governance, service delivery and support. Advise senior stakeholders, including CHROs, COOs and CFOs, on transformation strategy and priorities. Workday Advisory and System Selection Run HCM system selection exercises, including Workday against Oracle, SAP SuccessFactors and other platforms. Manage systems integrator (SI) procurement: write RFPs, set scoring criteria, run supplier demonstrations and lead evaluation. Review SI proposals, statements of work and commercial terms, and help clients negotiate a fair deal. Act as the client's independent adviser during implementation, providing quality assurance, design review and challenge to the SI. Delivery Plan and manage engagements to time, budget and quality, with clear reporting to clients and internal leadership. Support workstreams such as testing, data migration, change management, training and job architecture. Produce high quality client deliverables, including reports, presentations, evaluation packs and operating model designs. Workday Training for HR Teams Assess training needs across HR, payroll and people operations teams, and design a training plan that fits each role. Deliver Workday training to HR teams, both in person and online, covering core HCM processes, reporting and day to day administration. Create clear training materials, including user guides, quick reference cards, exercises and recorded walkthroughs. Prepare HR teams to support themselves after go live, including train the trainer sessions and handover to internal Workday support teams. Provide refresher and update training as Workday releases new features twice a year. Business Development and Practice Growth Build and maintain relationships with HR, finance and operations leaders across the US market. Identify new opportunities within existing clients and help shape proposals and pricing. Contribute to thought leadership, events and the development of our methods and tools. Coach and support more junior consultants. Skills and Experience: The right person will have at least eight years in HR transformation, with a strong track record on Workday programs. Essential At least eight years' experience in HR transformation, HR technology or HR operations, ideally with some of that time in consulting. Hands on involvement in at least two full Workday HCM implementations, either as a client lead, program manager or advisory partner. Sound knowledge of Workday HCM and how it fits with payroll, finance and other connected systems. Experience of running or supporting HCM system selection and SI procurement. Proven experience designing and delivering Workday training to HR teams, with the confidence to run sessions for groups at all levels. Good understanding of US HR and payroll practice, including multi state payroll and benefits administration. Confidence working with senior stakeholders and presenting to leadership teams. Excellent written skills, with the ability to produce clear, well-structured client reports. Desirable Experience in professional services firms, especially law firms, and an understanding of how partner and fee earner roles differ from standard employee models. Workday certification in HCM, Payroll, Compensation or Recruiting. Knowledge of Workday Payroll or third-party payroll providers such as ADP. Experience of global or cross border programs, including work with UK or European teams. A background in business development within a consulting firm. Other Qualities We want someone clients trust to tell them the truth, and colleagues enjoy working with. Independent and confident enough to challenge suppliers and clients when needed. Practical and focused on outcomes rather than theory. Comfortable working on your own in a growing market, while staying closely connected to a team across the US and UK. Curious, organized and able to manage several engagements at once. Commercially aware, with a genuine interest in helping the practice grow. About Us: Harbor is the preeminent provider of expert services across strategy, legal technology, operations, and intelligence. Our globally integrated team of 900+ strategists, technologists, and specialists navigate alongside our clients – leading law firms, corporations, and their law departments – to provide essential resources and invaluable insights. Anchored in a rich heritage of deep knowledge, steadfast relationships, and mutual respect, our unwavering dedication lies in shaping the future of the legal industry and fostering enduring partnerships within our community and ecosystem. Harbor is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, civil union status, national origin, ancestry, age, parental status, disabled status, veteran status, or any other legally protected classification, in accordance with applicable law.

jobs.jd: Who We Are Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management. We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it. You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries. jobs.title: 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting
jobs.jd: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team. You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company. They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month. You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft. Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue. You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual. If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI. Key responsibilities Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline. Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments. Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge. Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership. Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting. Serve as the primary contact for external auditors. Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready. Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer. Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close. Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close. Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements. Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326). Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments. Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries. Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence. Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes. Minimum qualifications Have strong ASC 606 knowledge, especially principal-vs-agent, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, and consumption-based revenue. Have owned a month-end close with tight deadlines and reviewed journal entries, reconciliations and flux analysis. Have built revenue reporting from large, imperfect third-party data sets and reconciled it to the general ledger. Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes. Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations. Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits. Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams. Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built. Preferred qualifications Have 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years managing revenue accounting or close teams. A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA). Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company. Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace). Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models. Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools. Experience with IPO readiness.
