jobs.title: Mercor AI Research Fund Grants: Economics of AI
jobs.jd:
ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.


MERCOR AI RESEARCH FUND GRANTS: ECONOMICS OF AI

One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical.

Mercor is seeking to fund AI research on the economic impacts of AI. This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply HERE https://www.mercor.com/careers/a0a98be0-d856-4129-b500-c0a3e412ef01/), our $5m of safety funding awards (apply HERE https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/mercor/1d59ce50-4207-4d95-b7fd-5a01e90b0897), and our funding of benchmarking research.

The grant supports:

 - The time of experts from Mercor's platform

 - Researcher hours

 - API costs

 - Stipends for event and conference attendance


BUDGET CATEGORIES

Applications are grouped into three budget tiers. Please state your tier clearly in your application and ensure your overall budget ask falls within it:

 - Tier 1: under $50,000: Suited to focused, well-scoped projects such as pilot studies, evaluations, replications, or extensions of existing work. These applications undergo a streamlined review.

 - Tier 2: under $200,000: Suited to substantial projects requiring dedicated personnel time, meaningful compute, or data collection. Reviewed with proportionally greater attention to the budget breakdown and implementation plan.

 - Tier 3: under $500,000: Reserved for ambitious, multi-component research programs. These applications receive the highest level of scrutiny: reviewers will expect a detailed justification of each spend category, a clear account of team capacity to execute at this scale, and milestones against which progress can be assessed.

The level of review scrutiny scales with the size of the ask, so applicants should request the smallest budget that credibly supports the proposed work.



 


RESEARCH AGENDA

 

We are interested in submissions in the following area:

1. Measuring AI’s impact on labor

 - How should we measure AI’s effect on real economic and labor outcomes — and what methodologies are up to the task?

 - To what extent do benchmark scores map onto real economic outcomes?

 - What is the right methodology for measuring AI’s impact on labor outcomes (employment, wages, task composition)?

 - How does occupational exposure to AI evolve over time, and how can novel datasets improve its measurement?



2. Human–AI collaboration and productivity

 - How do humans actually work with AI systems, and when does that collaboration make them more productive?

 - What is the efficiency gain of human experts when paired with AI models, and under what conditions?

 - How can we measure the “review cost” that model outputs impose on humans — the time and effort spent checking, correcting, and verifying AI work?

 - Which collaboration patterns improve output quality rather than merely output volume?



3. Enterprise adoption and returns

 - What does AI adoption look like inside organizations, and what returns does it generate?

 - How are organizations actually using AI, and how is that usage changing?

 - How can the effect of AI and agent deployments be measured causally, rather than through self-report or correlation?

 - What are the right enterprise-level variables for quantifying AI-driven productivity gains?



 


ELIGIBILITY

 

 - Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups (<20 people) that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.

 - Applicants must be based in the United States or the United Kingdom

We expect grantees to publish a paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.

 


TIMELINE

 

 - Application deadline: November 27, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (UTC−8)

 - Notification to applicants: by December 18, 2026

Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed. All applicants will be notified of the outcome whether or not they are shortlisted.

 
 


HOW TO APPLY

We invite interested researchers to submit a brief Expression of Interest (EOI) before preparing a full proposal. The EOI should be ~1–3 pages and include:

 - Research question and background (max 250 words): What are you trying to do? State your objective in plain language, with minimal jargon. How is this problem addressed today, and what are the limits of current practice? Who cares: if you succeed, what difference will it make, and to whom?

 - Project proposal (max 400 words): Concrete technical and implementation detail: your approach, methods, datasets, models, compute, and evaluation plan.

 - Novelty (max 200 words): What is new in your approach relative to existing and ongoing work, and why do you believe it will succeed where current practice falls short?

 - Risks (max 150 words): What are the main technical and execution risks, and how will you mitigate or detect them early?

 - Team (max 100 words; if the team is large, up to 200): The researchers on the project and their relevant background and prior work.

 - Proposed outcomes and timeline: Expected deliverables (papers, artifacts, datasets, tools) and key milestones, including how long the work will take. Include the mid-term and final “exams”: the checkpoints and success criteria by which we will know whether the project is on track and succeeds.

 - Budget overview: How much will it cost? Provide a specific overall budget ask, your budget tier (see Budget Categories), and a breakdown by spend category (e.g., personnel, compute, data, travel/other).
   
   - Other sources of funding for this project should be clearly identified in the proposal budget




GUIDANCE FOR APPLICANTS.

 - Strong EOIs are specific rather than high-level: they name the methods, systems, and evaluation criteria they will use, and they engage directly with existing literature and ongoing efforts rather than describing the problem space in general terms.

 - The EOI should briefly establish the PI’s (and key team members’) relevant background and prior work; proposals without demonstrated expertise in the research area are rarely competitive. Researchers with experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, and post-training are encouraged to apply

 - Proposals that duplicate work already being pursued by many other groups are unlikely to advance unless they offer a clearly differentiated angle.

 - Please do not include confidential or proprietary information in your Expression of Interest. Submitting an Expression of Interest does not obligate Mercor to make an award.

 
 


AWARD TERMS

Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:

jobs.title: Agent Post-Training, Computer Use Research
jobs.jd:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Agent Post-Training team creates the frontier agents OpenAI ships to the world. We are training the models behind our agents in Codex, ChatGPT, the API, and other frontier products: persistent, proactive intelligence that can operate computers, collaborate with people and other agents, and expand what people and organizations can imagine, attempt, and achieve.

We define what the next generation of agents should be able to do, build the training signal that teaches those abilities, and run the experiments that make them real. Our work spans coding, tool use, computer use, multi-agent coordination, long-horizon execution, factuality, instruction following, calibrated reasoning, and taste.

Our team is where new model capabilities get made. We build the data, environments, graders, training methods, and feedback loops that shape what OpenAI's next agents can do, then carry those capabilities through major training runs and into the products people use.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a member of Agent Post-Training, Computer Use, you will teach models to operate computers. You will help train models that can navigate browsers and desktops, use tools and applications, reason through complex workflows, collaborate with users and other agents, and complete long-horizon tasks with reliability and judgment. This work sits at the intersection of frontier model training, product behavior, evaluation, and systems engineering, and will directly shape the computer-use capabilities shipped in OpenAI’s next generation of agents. Currently, our models are the best in the world at this behavior!

You will work with researchers, engineers, product teams, infrastructure teams, and safety/alignment partners to decide what should go into major model runs, measure whether it worked, and ship improvements into products used by real people. This is a high-agency role for people who want their work to land directly in frontier models.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU MIGHT

 - Design and run experiments that improve agentic model behavior for complex computer use https://openai.com/index/codex-for-almost-everything/, including desktop and browser.

 - Own end-to-end improvements to the post-training stack, including RL, data pipelines, graders, reward signals, evals, diagnostics, and model-behavior analysis.

 - Build evals and environments that expose the next set of model failures, then turn those failures into training data, product fixes, or new research directions.

 - Partner with Codex and ChatGPT product teams to understand what users need and translate product signal into model improvements.

 - Work on early-training and alignment interventions, including data mixtures, objectives, synthetic data, and eval loops that shape downstream agent behavior.

 - Help decide which integrations, capabilities, and fixes are ready for inclusion in major model runs.

 - Improve the machinery for large-scale training and launch: experiment velocity, reliability, observability, reproducibility, cost, latency, and production readiness.

 - Take on cross-functional projects that touch model training, product infrastructure, and the production agent harness, such as multi-agent systems or training directly against production-like environments.

 - Debug hard failures in shipped or near-shipped models and turn messy qualitative behavior into concrete hypotheses, experiments, and fixes.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have strong technical fundamentals in machine learning, software engineering, systems, statistics, or a related field, and can learn quickly across the parts you have not worked in before.

 - Have hands-on experience with LLMs, RL, RLHF/RLAIF, post-training, evals, graders, synthetic data, model training, coding agents, tool-using agents, or production ML systems.

 - Are excited by open-ended problems where the path is unclear, the signal is noisy, and the right answer requires both research taste and engineering execution.

 - Care about product impact and model behavior, not just benchmark movement. You have opinions about what makes an agent useful, reliable, honest, tasteful, and easy to work with.

 - Can move from a vague behavioral problem to a concrete experiment: define the hypothesis, build the pipeline, run the model, analyze the result, and decide what to do next.

 - Are comfortable working across research, product, infrastructure, data, evals, and safety boundaries, and can communicate clearly with each group.

 - Like building load-bearing systems and processes when that is what the team needs, even if the work is not glamorous.

 - Want to train and ship the models that make agents genuinely useful for developers, enterprises, researchers, and everyday users.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

We are backed by a powerhouse of industry-leading Board of Directors and Advisory Council Members who are passionate, hands-on, and dive into the important work with us.
 
Learn more atprojecthealthyminds.com and @projecthealthyminds on social.
 
About The Engagement
 
• Based in the US (ideally NYC)
• ~20 hours a week, set with the Services Research Manager.
• Initial 90-day contract, with the option to extend as we add locations.
 
About The Role
 
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
 
People come to Project Healthy Minds to find mental health services they can trust. We're growing – going beyond national services and building local listings. Each listing has to get the details right: the address, the hours, who the service is for, expectations around costs, and whether the service meets the screening criteria our Clinical Advisory Committee (CAC) sets for that type of service. You'll do the research behind those listings, working with our Services Research Manager to grow our services directory.
 
WHAT YOU'LL DO
 
• Verify and complete service records: address, hours, contact details, costs, insurance, and other tags in our data model.
• Label services against our screening criteria, quoting the evidence for each answer. 
• Find services we don't list yet as we build each new location.
• Note any service that doesn't fit our data model and explain what doesn't fit.
 
WHAT YOU'LL BRING
 
• You've done research where accuracy mattered and you had to cite your sources, such as at a 211 or resource directory, in fact-checking, on a civic data team, or in a library.
• You're comfortable contacting organizations you don't know and getting clear answers from whoever responds.
• You follow a written procedure closely, and you speak up when it doesn't fit what you're finding.
• You're organized in spreadsheets and careful with details.
• You're comfortable with AI tools and check their output before you trust it.
• You care about the person on the other end: someone looking for help, often on a hard day, who can't afford a wrong phone number or a clinic that closed last year.
 
NICE TO HAVE
 
• Spanish or another language besides English.
• Training in social work, counseling, or public health, or experience working in mental health services.
 
The hourly rate for this role is $25 to $40, depending on experience.
  
Due to the high volume of applications received, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. We ask for a short paid work sample so we can see how you research a real service and handle the judgment calls. We review this over a live video call.

jobs.title: Executive Operations Leader
jobs.jd:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.



Plaid’s Executive Assistant (EA) team sits within the People Team and partners closely with the company’s most senior leaders. Our EAs are trusted, strategic partners who help leaders stay focused on their highest-impact work—from managing complex calendars and preparing for critical meetings to coordinating Board logistics, leadership offsites, customer dinners, and company-wide events. We operate as one connected team, sharing best practices, supporting one another, and exploring new technology and AI-enabled approaches to make the way we work faster, smarter, and more effective.



As the EA Team Lead, you’ll lead and develop a team of EAs who support senior leaders across Plaid, while also directly supporting one of our C-Suite executives. You’ll set clear standards, bring consistency and best practices to high-impact areas such as leadership rhythms, onsite planning, and company events, and serve as a trusted partner to executives and People Team leaders. You’ll also help evolve and scale the function through new approaches to technology, AI, and automation.



Responsibilities

 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of EAs through regular 1:1s, candid feedback, goal setting, and career development.

 - Provide direct support for one C-Suite Executive and back up coverage as needed.

 - Set the vision and operating standards for the EA program, including onboarding, role expectations, coverage, and ways of working.

 - Build scalable playbooks, templates, and repeatable approaches for leadership meetings, onsite planning, All Hands, company events, and other high-impact programs.

 - Foster a connected EA community through shared practices, knowledge sharing, and thoughtful coverage across the team.

 - Partner with executives and their EAs to understand priorities, calibrate support, and ensure the right level of coverage.

 - Own hiring for the EA team, including defining the bar, partnering with Recruiting, and onboarding new hires.

 - Identify and implement efficiencies through technology, AI, and automation to improve how the team works.

 - Serve as an escalation point and thought partner for complex, sensitive, or cross-functional situations.

 - Partner with the People Team on programs and initiatives involving executive and leadership support.



Qualifications

 - 8+ years of experience as an EA supporting C-suite executives in complex, fast-paced environments.

 - 3-5 years of experience leading, coaching, or managing EAs or administrative teams.

 - A track record of developing people, with the ability to give clear, direct feedback and help others grow.

 - Experience planning and running complex programs and events, such as leadership onsites, Board meetings, All Hands, and company events.

 - A strategic and operational mindset, with the ability to turn recurring work into scalable, repeatable systems.

 - Strong judgment and discretion when handling confidential and sensitive information.

 - Ability to build trust and influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners without relying on authority.

 - Builder mindset, with comfort using technology, AI, and automation to improve how work gets done.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

 - Comfort operating at a fast pace, navigating shifting priorities, and working flexibly when the needs of the business require it.

jobs.title: Financial Systems Admin
jobs.jd:
KAYAK, part of Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG), is a leading travel search engine. With billions of queries across our platforms, we help people find their perfect flight, stay, rental car and vacation package. We're also transforming business travel with a new corporate travel solution, KAYAK for Business.

As an employee of KAYAK, you will be part of a travel company that operates a portfolio of global metasearch brands including Momondo, Cheapflights and HotelsCombined, among others. From start-up to industry leader, innovation is in our DNA and every employee has an opportunity to make their mark. Our focus is on building the best travel search engine to make it easier for everyone to experience the world.

KAYAK is looking for a NetSuite / Salesforce / FloQast Administrator to join our Enterprise Applications team within Finance. You'll be the day-to-day owner of configuration, user administration, and integration health across our core finance and revenue systems — the person who actually knows why a saved search broke, why a workflow stalled, or why a sync between NetSuite and Salesforce didn't fire. This role rewards curiosity and precision: you don't need to arrive as a NetSuite expert, but you do need to want to become one, and you need to be the kind of person who double-checks a config change before it touches production. You'll work closely with Finance, Accounting, Sales Ops, and Engineering, and partner with senior systems analysts and architects on the bigger roadmap items — but the daily craft of keeping these systems accurate, well-documented, and running smoothly is yours.

This role will be required to work from our Concord, MA or Cambridge, MA office at least 3 days per week.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Administer day-to-day configuration of NetSuite, Salesforce, FloQast and Blackline: user setup/deactivation, roles and permissions, saved searches, SuiteAnalytics workbooks/dashboards, Salesforce flows and validation rules, troubleshooting issues within Salesforce.

 - Serve as backup administrator for Expensify, supporting user provisioning, system configuration, synchronization issues, and end-user troubleshooting

 - Build and maintain NetSuite SuiteFlow workflows and troubleshoot existing SuiteScript customizations — you don't need to write scripts from scratch on day one, but you should be comfortable reading one, tracing what it does, and knowing when to escalate to a developer.

 - Triage and resolve support tickets from Finance and general employees related to expense reports, financial records, and account access, digging into root cause rather than just closing the ticket.

 - Monitor and troubleshoot integrations between NetSuite and Salesforce — including iPaaS/middleware tools and direct API/SFTP data feeds — escalating to engineering when needed.

 - Support month-end and quarter-end close by ensuring system data accuracy, running reports, and resolving reconciliation discrepancies.

 - Support the month-end close by managing file-based data transfers to the external reporting platform, validating successful loads, and troubleshooting exceptions with the Reporting team

 - Perform sandbox testing and validate NetSuite's release upgrades against existing customizations and integrations before anything touches production.

 - Maintain user access lists and perform basic access reviews to support audit, SOX, and compliance needs.

 - Create and maintain clear documentation, quick-reference guides, and training materials — you take pride in writing something a new teammate could actually follow without asking you a follow-up question.

 - Partner with senior systems analysts/architects to implement approved process changes and provide hands-on support during testing and hypercare for larger rollouts, without owning roadmap prioritization.




PLEASE APPLY IF YOU HAVE:

 - 2-4 years of hands-on administration experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, and/or Expensify (or similar ERP/CRM/expense platforms) — OR strong ERP/CRM administration fundamentals elsewhere plus genuine enthusiasm for going deep on NetSuite specifically. We'd rather hire for curiosity and a learning mindset than a perfect checklist of prior tools.

 - Familiarity with (or eagerness to quickly learn) NetSuite's configuration layer: saved searches, SuiteFlow, roles/permissions, custom fields and records, and at least reading-level comfort with SuiteScript.

 - Working knowledge of basic system integrations (API/SFTP, or iPaaS tools like Celigo/Workato/Boomi) and comfort troubleshooting data sync issues.

 - Real attention to detail — the kind that notices a saved search is returning one extra row before it becomes a finance reporting problem.

 - Solid Excel/Google Sheets skills; comfort building reports and saved searches.

 - Clear communicator who can support non-technical end users and explain system issues in plain language.

 - Familiarity with basic finance/accounting workflows (AP, expense management, order-to-cash) is a plus but not required.

 - Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent practical experience; NetSuite/Salesforce admin certifications (e.g. NetSuite SuiteFoundation, Salesforce Administrator) are a plus and a good signal of the self-directed learning this role rewards.




BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year.

 - Company-wide week off a year – the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)

 - No meeting Fridays

 - Paid parental leave

 - Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday

 - Paid volunteer time

 - Focus on your career growth:

 - Development Dollars

 - Leadership development

 - Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings

 - Travel Discounts

 - Employee Resource Groups

 - Competitive retirement and health plans

 - Free lunch 2 days per week

 - Focus on mental health and well-being:

 - Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth

 - Company-paid subscription to HeadSpace

There are a variety of factors that go into determining a salary range, including but not limited to external market benchmark data, geographic location, and years of experience sought/required. The range for this Massachusetts-based role is $85,000-$100,000.

We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including: health benefits; flexible spending account; retirement benefits; life insurance; paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays and paid holidays); and parental leave benefits. This role is eligible to be considered for an annual bonus.

 


INCLUSION

At KAYAK, we want everyone to have the space to grow, share ideas and do great work. That's why we're focused on hiring the best talent from all walks of life and experiences, supporting them well and making sure no one feels like they have to fit a mold to belong here.

Need any adjustments for the interview, application or on the job? No problem – just give us a heads-up. We've got you.

GROWTH, FIELD (AMER WEST) @ CLAY

We’re looking for a Growth, Field to be the “local CMO” for our AMER West sales region. About half of Clay’s business now runs through a sales-led motion serving mid-market, enterprise, and strategic accounts, and our field team gets those accounts in a room with our sellers. We already have dedicated field coverage for AMER East. In this role, you’ll build the same for the West: third-party tradeshows that source net-new pipeline, and hosted dinners and executive events that accelerate and expand existing deals. You’ll work closely with the AMER West sales leadership team and report to our Head of Field Marketing. From day one you’ll own a full region end to end, and you’ll be measured on the pipeline you source and the return on every dollar you spend.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Stand up the AMER West program calendar and target-account list with regional sales leadership, then run the first wave of tradeshows and dinners against it.

 - Decide with sellers where event budget goes for the best ROI. Budget moves between regions based on performance, so you’ll report sourced pipeline, acceleration and expansion impact, and cost per opportunity for every program.

 - Be sales’ best friend day to day. Get reps excited to invite the right people to dinners, equip them with invite templates and target lists, and drive follow-up on tradeshow leads until they turn into meetings and opportunities.

 - Set up a steady working rhythm with AMER West sales managers and directors, covering planning, pipeline reviews, and post-event retros.

 - Partner with your AMER East counterpart so the two regions share a consistent cadence, playbook, and reporting.

 - Use agents and automation to run programs leaner than the headcount suggests. As the team grows, help shape scope for future field marketers in the region.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 4–8 years in field or regional marketing at a B2B company with a meaningful sales-led motion, ideally acting as the marketing lead for a specific sales region.

 - A track record of running both third-party tradeshows and hosted first-party dinners or executive events, and the pipeline numbers to show for it.

 - Comfort owning a budget and being judged on sourced pipeline, cost per opportunity, and ROI.

 - Credibility with sellers and sales leaders. You know how to get reps bought in and following through, not just showing up.

 - Obsessive execution: you deliver polished events at volume without losing sight of the pipeline behind them.

 - Operational rigor: you build target lists, invite plans, and follow-up plays before you book venues.

 - You are AI forward: you use agents and automation to plan, promote, and follow up on programs efficiently.

 - Strongly preferred: experience building in Clay.

jobs.jd: Austal USA Advanced Technologies (AT) is a division of Austal USA, a global defense contractor that designs and manufactures surface and subsurface vessels. Austal USA AT works at the forefront of shipbuilding to invent, mature, and implement advanced maritime technologies which enhance operational capacities and improve defense system readiness. Austal USA AT operates a technology hub in Charlottesville, VA, and the U.S. Navy’s Additive Manufacturing Center of Excellence (AM COE) located in Danville, VA. The mission of the AM COE is to operationalize additive manufacturing in the submarine industrial base and provide emergent request support to sustain our Nation’s fleet. As a Applications Support Analyst II, you’ll play a pivotal role in the overseeing the digital tools deployed at the Navy’s AM COE in Danville, and the advanced manufacturing facility in Charlottesville. Key responsibilities include managing the digital manufacturing system platforms and safeguarding the Navy’s central repository for AM manufacturing data. As a member of our team, you’ll be part of a dynamic environment where creativity, expertise, and impact converge. We invite you to join us in building the next generation of submarines. MUST BE LOCAL to Danville OR Charlottesville, VA REPORTS TO: Program Manager, Digital Solutions LOCATION : Danville OR Charlottesville, VA SUPERVISES: N/A PURPOSE: The Applications Support Analyst II will evaluate the Advanced Technologies division’s existing software and application setup, identifying areas for potential improvement, and apply changes to applications. This role supports higher-complexity issues with moderate supervision, focusing on the configuration, maintenance, and integration of applications to align with user requirements and organizational objectives related to budget, efficiency, and productivity. DUTIES / RESPONSIBILITIES: Oversee the installation, configuration, troubleshooting, maintenance, and implementation of new and existing computer and software applications deployed for the US Navy AM COE. Research, evaluate, and recommend new software and updates for existing applications to improve US Navy AM COE processes. Conduct in-depth assessments by gathering data, analyzing system and business requirements, and developing improvement plans for US Navy AM COE digital tools. Utilize advanced application specific knowledge to configure, update, and debug US Navy AM COE applications to maintain end-to-end solutions. Provide support for COTS applications (driven by documented specifications provided through lead department personnel) and reports to implement new business requirements and augment current application functionality across US Navy AM COE systems. Offer ongoing support to US Navy AM COE application users by diagnosing and resolving technical issues; escalate complex problems to senior team members as necessary. Ensure data integrity through data quality control, validation, and documentation; assists in developing requirements for program and operational initiatives. Create and execute test scripts independently, as needed for program tasks, with minimal oversight. Collaborate with senior team members on feasibility analysis, project scopes, and work with the Program Management team to prioritize deliverables, and product functionality negotiations. Maintain documentation for recordkeeping, change control and configuration maintenance. Provide analytic support regarding data interpretation from DB supplied queries. Partners with AM COE team to provide routine reporting on software solution performance. Participates in Integration Testing, User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Functionality Testing for US Navy AM COE digital tools. Other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS / KNOWLEDGE / EXPERIENCE: Required: High School Diploma or equivalent required. Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field required. A combination of education and experience may be accepted in lieu of a degree. 3 - 5 years’ experience in Applications Support or similar role. At least 1 year of directly related experience managing PLM, MES, and/or ERP systems. Intermediate understanding of software applications, IT support principles, and troubleshooting techniques. Proficient in Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel and Visio). Demonstrated working knowledge of computers, software applications, and systems maintenance. Ability to work effectively in an ever-changing environment. Good written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated working knowledge of organizing and coordinating scheduled events (meetings, team-based tasks). Excellent interpersonal and presentation skills. Ability to exhibit the following characteristics in everyday work: leadership to assigned initiatives, analytical problem-solving, risk identification/mitigation, sense of urgency; sense of accountability; excellent communication (listening and effective speaking), relationship-building. Preferred: Experience in manufacturing or a related industry is preferred. Proficient/Experience with one or more of the following is preferred: Workday. AutoCAD WindChill PLM MES. Machine Learning/AI. ADDITIONAL GUIDELINES: Candidates must meet the following employment eligibility guidelines to be considered for employment with Austal USA: 18 years of age or older at time of application. Able to provide proof of US Person Status. The ability to obtain and maintain a DoD clearance may be required if deemed necessary in the scope of your position responsibilities. No felony convictions of Theft/Deception or Violent crimes within seven years from disposition date. No felony convictions of Drug crimes within three years from disposition date. Willing to submit to a drug screen. Willing to submit to a background check. TOOLS: Microsoft Office Excel and Word DIRECTION EXERCISED: N/A DISCRETION EXERCISED : Moderate discretion when addressing application issues and troubleshooting user problems. The role involves independently resolving a broader range of issues using established procedures and knowledge, while exercising judgment to determine when complex or non-standard problems require escalation to senior support teams for further resolution. LIASES WITH: IT and Business Integration Staff, Supply Chain and Purchasing. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS : The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Must be able to tour all vessels and work sites. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, use hands to manipulate, handle, or feel, reach with hands and arms, climb and balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl, and talk or hear. Specific physical requirements include the following: Must have the ability to bend, squat, stoop, crawl, and kneel. Lift/push/pull up to 50lbs on an occasional basis. Lift/push/pull up to 20lbs on a frequent basis. Must have the ability to climb in a safe manner (climbing as a minimum includes stairs and ramps). SAFETY: Must comply with company, federal, state, and local safety and environmental rules and regulations while performing daily job tasks. Austal’s commitment to equal employment opportunity applies at all levels of employment, in all job titles, including the executive level, and to all employment actions, including but not limited to decisions concerning recruitment, hiring, training, and promotion.

jobs.title: Load Modeling and Development Analyst
jobs.jd: At ERCOT, our diverse and dynamic work environment provides a platform on which employees can work together to build the future of the Texas power grid and wholesale market utilizing the latest technologies and resources. We encourage you to join our talented, dedicated workforce to develop world-class solutions for today and tomorrow’s energy challenges while learning new skills and growing your career. ERCOT is committed to fostering inclusion at all levels of our company. It is the cornerstone of our corporate values of accountability, leadership, innovation, trust, and expertise. We know that individuals with a wide variety of talents, ideas, and experiences propel the innovation that drives our success. An inclusive and diverse workforce strengthens us and allows for a collaborative environment to solve the challenges that face our industry today and in the future. JOB SUMMARY Provides analysis and technical support for ERCOT’s operational and planning load forecasting processes to ensure continuing reliable operations of the electric power grid in compliance with NERC Standards, ERCOT Protocols and Market Guides. Implements appropriate demand and load forecasting modeling, develops tools and procedures to monitor forecast performance, input data quality, model outputs, weather and demand conditions in support of system operators. Develop solutions for current or future demand and load forecasting issues and appropriately reports findings and recommendations. Supports the evaluation and adoption of advanced analytics and emerging forecasting tools to improve forecast quality, situational awareness, and operational decision support. JOB DUTIES Operational Load Forecasting — Level 2 / Level 3 Understands the basic principles, theories and concepts related to the profession and learns how to apply them within the ERCOT culture. Follows standard practices and procedures in analyzing situations or data from which answers can be readily obtained. Contributes to specific objectives and outcomes as directed. ADDITIONAL JOB DUTIES Operational Load Forecasting — Level 2 / Level 3 Provides technical expertise to the ISO and Load Forecasting team for operational and planning load forecast analysis, including forecast production support, monitoring, and performance review. Supports the development, testing, implementation, documentation, and training of load forecasting methodologies, models, tools, and procedures. Exercises judgment within defined procedures and practices to determine appropriate action. Supports load forecasting model runs, data quality checks, input/output validation, and historical database updates. Reviews and analyzes historical load, weather, calendar, and operational event data from ERCOT and other relevant independent sources to validate, maintain, and improve statistical and time-series load forecasting models. Creates estimates for the ERCOT Control Area annual energy and monthly, daily, hourly, and peak models that involve economic forecasts, historical database updates and maintenance. Develops and enhances demand response models, and other energy models, including plug-in electric vehicles, distributed generation models, and other load modifier models. Develops and maintains forecast performance metrics, reports, dashboards, and recurring analyses. Supports analysis used to develop recommendations to Planning and/or Operations onload forecast, demand response, load modifier impacts, forecast uncertainty, and operational forecast risks, in coordination with the Operational Load Forecasting Lead, supervisor, or manager as appropriate. Provides load forecast and demand response recommendations to Operations, in coordination with the Operational Load Forecasting Lead, supervisor, or manager as appropriate. Assists in developing economic-driven forecasting analytics, decision-support tools, processes, and procedures that enhance forecast performance, input data quality, model review, and departmental efficiencies. Participates in multifunctional teams to obtain input, address comments, and support load forecasting studies, methodology changes, and process improvements. Maintains knowledge of emerging trends and industry best practices applicable to load forecasting, operational forecasting, and forecast analytics. EXPERIENCE Experience with load forecasting, weather-driven analytics, statistical or time-series modeling, large datasets, and data analysis tools such as Python, R, SQL, SAS, Excel, Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools is preferred. Operational Load Forecasting — Level 2 / Level 3 Level 2: Requires minimum 1 year job-related work experience in excess of degree requirements. Level 3: Requires minimum 3 years job-related work experience in excess of degree requirements. EDUCATION Bachelor’s Degree: Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or Engineering required. Master’s Degree: Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or Engineering preferred. A combination of education and experience that provides equivalent knowledge to a major in such fields is required. jobs.title: Security Operations Analyst (Tier 2)
jobs.jd: At Aristocrat, we are passionate about delivering world-class gaming experiences that bring happiness to millions of players worldwide. We are seeking an exceptionally skilled Security Operations Analyst (Tier 2) to join our team. As part of our Security Operations Center, you will play a crucial role in protecting our digital assets and maintaining our flawless security standards. This position offers an outstanding opportunity to collaborate with global teams, grow within a structured mentoring program, and build your career in a modern SOC environment. If you are ambitious and ready to compete at the highest level, this role is for you! What You'll Do Own MSSP customer concerns and medium/high-severity alerts from start to finish. Scope the activity and build the timeline. Identify indicators of compromise (IOCs) and investigate endpoint, identity, network, and cloud data to reach a defensible conclusion. Review a sample of MSSP triage for quality, offering tuning, detection-gap, and escalation-criteria feedback to the MSSP. Triage phishing (header analysis, sandboxing), malware (static & sandbox), and credential-compromise investigations. Complete containment and remediation within approved playbooks — host isolation, account disablement, credential reset, IOC blocking — and record every action taken. Raise issues to senior specialists with a full set of information: hypothesis, evidence, actions taken, current risk, and specific ask; send well-understood benign patterns back to the MSSP along with a detailed disposition and the missing playbook step. Build and run queries across our SIEM, EDR, and SOAR platforms and MSSP tooling to support investigations and reporting. Identify detection and tuning gaps. Flag false positives and propose tuning, suppression, or enrichment with supporting evidence. Test and validate detection changes shipped by the detection engineering team. Document every case to a high standard. Ensure it is complete, accurate, and reproducible by someone not on shift. Accept peer and lead QA review. Act on feedback within the same cycle. Support specialist-led threat hunts and incident response — evidence gathering and technical analysis from detection through root cause analysis (RCA). Contribute to playbook, runbook, and knowledge-base improvements drawn from your own casework. Participate in the 24x7 rotating shift roster, including on-call and occasional weekend coverage. What We're Looking For 2+ years of hands-on SOC / security operations experience, with ownership of investigations beyond initial triage. A bachelor's degree in information systems, cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Query proficiency on our CrowdStrike stack — CrowdStrike Query Language (CQL) — or transferable SIEM query experience (e.g., KQL, SPL); plus hands-on EDR (live response, process-tree analysis, host isolation). Working knowledge of Windows, Linux, and Active Directory (AD) / Entra ID attack patterns; comfortable reading authentication, process, and network logs without a playbook. A solid grasp of the incident-response process, phishing and malware investigations; MITRE ATT&CK for mapping observed behavior. Nice to have: Security+, ISC2 SSCP, Microsoft SC-200, CrowdStrike (CCFA/CCFR), Blue Team Level 1/2 (BTL1/BTL2), GCIA, GCIH, or CySA+ certifications. Cloud security monitoring (AWS, Azure, or GCP); scripting (Python or PowerShell); SOAR/automation. Exposure to detection tuning or threat hunting. Join us at Aristocrat and be part of a team that strives for excellence in every aspect of our operations. Together, we can achieve great things and make an impact on the gaming community worldwide! jobs.title: Quality Control Analyst II
jobs.jd: The Quality Control Analyst II role is responsible for performing environmental monitoring, RODI water sampling and testing, microbiological and analytical QC assays, documentation review, and support of deviations, out-of-specification results, environmental excursions, investigations, and trend evaluations in accordance with approved SOPs, ISO 14644 cleanroom controls, and the company’s ISO 9001 Quality Management System. The Quality Control Analyst II reports directly to the Quality Control Manager and supports routine QC laboratory operations within ISO-classified cleanrooms and controlled laboratory environments. This is a 100% on site position. Primary responsibilities include: Perform routine environmental monitoring of ISO-classified cleanroom and controlled environments, including collection, documentation, and review of data to support trend analysis. Collect and test RODI water samples in accordance with approved procedures and established testing requirements. Perform routine QC laboratory testing, including pH, conductivity, endotoxin, bioburden, and related microbiological or analytical assays. Accurately document test results, sample collection details, observations, and anomalies in controlled records using good documentation practices. Follow approved SOPs, work instructions, laboratory safety practices, gowning requirements, and contamination control procedures. Initiate, write, review, and support deviations, out-of-specification results, environmental excursions, and related laboratory investigations as assigned. Review peer documentation, laboratory data, and controlled records for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with approved procedures. Support SOP creation, revision, periodic review, and implementation of controlled laboratory and cleanroom procedures. Support cleanroom monitoring program maintenance, environmental trend evaluations, and continuous improvement activities as needed. Qualifications and Skills: · Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, or a related scientific discipline required; 2+ years of Quality Control laboratory experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience, preferred. Work Experience Requirements: · Experience working in ISO-classified cleanroom environments, including ISO Class 7 and/or ISO Class 8 areas, preferred. · Working knowledge of ISO 14644 cleanroom practices, contamination control expectations, environmental monitoring requirements, and routine cleanroom behavior. · Hands-on experience performing environmental monitoring, RODI water sampling/testing, pH, conductivity, bioburden, endotoxin, and related QC laboratory testing. · Strong aseptic technique with the ability to consistently follow gowning, cleaning, sampling, laboratory safety, and contamination control procedures. · Ability to work efficiently within an ISO 9001 Quality Management System while following approved procedures and maintaining accurate, compliant records. · Strong attention to detail with demonstrated ability to complete documentation accurately and in accordance with approved SOPs, work instructions, and good documentation practices. · Ability to review laboratory data, test results, and controlled records for completeness, accuracy, and compliance. · Experience supporting deviations, out-of-specification results, environmental excursions, investigations, and trend evaluations preferred. · Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly document results, write reports, and collaborate cross-functionally. · Ability to work independently once trained, prioritize daily laboratory activities, and escalate issues appropriately. · Experience mentoring, training, or providing technical guidance to junior analysts preferred. · Experience with equipment qualification/validation activities, SAP, CaneaOne, or other quality and documentation systems preferred. Physical Requirements: Regularly required to bend, reach, stand, walk or sit daily Ability to move and lift objects up to 50 pounds, with assistance or other aids where appropriate. Our mission is to inspire advances in bioprocessing as a trusted partner in the production of biologic drugs that improve human health worldwide. Focused on cost and process efficiencies, we deliver innovative technologies and solutions that help set new standards in bioprocessing. The estimated hourly rate/salary range for this role, based in the United States of America is $31/Hr,-$38/Hr.. Compensation decisions are dependent on several factors including, but not limited to an individual's qualifications, location, internal equity, and alignment with market data. Additionally, employees are eligible to participate in one of our variable cash programs (bonus or commission) and eligible roles may receive equity as part of the compensation package. We offer a wide range of benefits such as paid time off, health/dental/vision, retirement benefits and flexible spending accounts. All compensation and benefits information will be confirmed in writing at the time of offer.
